assignment_statements.text:
**Case and dockets:** Jeffries v. Harleston; Second Circuit No. 93-7876; no separate Supreme Court docket assigned.
**Event and date:** Plenary merits decision on authorized submission, 1997-11-17; October Term 1997.
**Result:** Appellate judgment vacated and case remanded, 6–3 as to vacatur; the bounded mandate commands five votes. Stone-Zsela would require a limited new trial on his different substantive rule.
**Version / lineage:** Original decision of this Run; durable file-based preservation under the no-Git instruction. No earlier completed Record is superseded.

The July 1991 Albany address was off campus, unaffiliated with CUNY, and neither assigned nor controlled as a duty. Jeffries was introduced by his chair title. His actual functions included records, course assignments, meetings, internal representation, budget assistance and tenure evaluations; the supported record describes a nonpolicymaking role without special public-contact or confidentiality duties. Administrative assessments reported adequate performance, not flawless performance. Recruitment, fundraising, faculty interaction and community relationships were identified institutional concerns. The jury found both no actual disruption and reasonable expectation of disruption; neither finding replaces the other. The 1995 panel performed a legal balance and separately treated nine successful votes as an independent cause. It did not merely omit balancing.

One signed plenary opinion addresses the two grounds and distinct mandate, with separate writings explaining the genuine substantive/remedial divisions. Parts are fixed by those differences before assignment. The actual earlier tables show **Stone-Zsela 0; Stevens 0; O'Connor 0; Scalia 1; Kennedy 0; Souter 0; Thomas 0; Ginsburg 1; Breyer 0**. Last counted event is Khan; Brown and Monroe are excluded. These counts are freshly used for each part's assignment, with no part of this unwritten Record counted early.

Stone is in the vacatur coalition and assigns Parts I and II. Part I's eligible full-join authors and minimum-plus-one pool are **Stevens, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer**; minimum zero. Stone is ineligible because his approved substantive rule differs. Part II's eligible authors and pool add **Stone-Zsela**, who fully joins its exact actual-cause propositions; minimum remains zero. Stone chooses **Souter** for both: his precise Waters endpoint treatment and Umbehr counterfactual analysis directly fit coordination of a role-sensitive balance with personal causal proof without an investigation code. Kennedy offers a strong alternative on genuine grounds, but Souter's coupled endpoint/counterfactual treatment supplies the concrete fit advantage. Stone's distinct categorical ground prevents self-assignment of Part I.

Stone does not belong to the five-member bounded-mandate coalition. **Stevens**, its senior Justice, assigns Part III to **Souter**, who fully supports every mandate qualification and can keep the corrective grounds and available defenses coherent. The Chief's balance rule does not bind that Associate assignment; the same actual counts and five fully compatible authors are recorded. A single eligible Justice carries every part, so no divided authorship is created. No commitment is revised to obtain an author.

Stone treats the address as citizen speech as a matter of law and would narrow doctrine to exclude offense, hostility, reputational consequences and predicted disruption consisting of reactions to its viewpoint as grounds for punishment. He permits discipline for assigned official speech and independently proved regulable misconduct. He rejects blanket superseding cause and applies Mt. Healthy defendant by defendant. He requires a new trial limited to causation, independently lawful same-decision grounds, immunity and relief; he would not reinstate inconsistent verdicts or decide damages and immunity now. His Part II join is confined to the compatible causal propositions and application, with the substantive predicate and remedy separately stated. He does not join Parts I or III. No approved core is narrowed, no new investigatory duty is attributed to him, and no fallback is used.

## Adaptive audit annex

## 1. United States v. Kirk — February 14, 1998

### Component commitments

**Result:** All eight Associates would affirm the judgment sustaining Count One against the granted Commerce Clause challenge. The common ground applies Hale's possession/transfer integration rule to prohibited stock produced by local conversion. It does not turn the dismissed transfer counts or the reported sale narrative into elements of the possession conviction.

**Operative proposition:** Congress may include the knowing possession of this completed, converted post-ban machinegun in §922(o)'s prohibition on additions to the civilian machinegun stock because excluding the locally created stock from the possession prohibition would permit its retention, concealment, acquisition, and continued availability for circulation, materially impairing the valid transfer/stock regime. That sufficient Commerce and Necessary and Proper connection does not require a transaction-specific interstate crossing or an additional judicially created commerce element.

| Justice | Reconciled judgment and adopted ground | Date-eligible individual basis; material join boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Stevens | Affirm Count One on the common Hale application. | Joined Hale Part I and Rybar Part I. No need to adopt the lower court's broader gun-crime or drug-trade aggregation theory; the narrower existing rule independently sustains this conviction. |
| O'Connor | Affirm on integrated prohibited-stock regulation. | Authored Hale Part I; joined Lopez's connection-before-magnitude rule and Rybar Part I. Local conversion adds stock to the regulated class; judicially identifiable impairment, not general enforcement convenience, is essential. |
| Scalia | Affirm under the enacted possession prohibition and Hale's necessary-inclusion ground. | Joined Lopez, Hale Part I, and Rybar Part I. Refuses an invented interstate element or affirmance treating dismissed transfers as the offense of conviction. |
| Kennedy | Affirm; the operative class is prohibited machinegun stock, including the completed converted weapon here. | Authored Rybar's unanimous commerce application and joined Hale and Lopez. Rybar's sale facts made its application concrete but did not establish a universal proved-sale condition. |
| Souter | Affirm on the common ground without reopening broader Commerce questions. | Joined Hale Part I and Rybar Part I. Congress's practical design latitude operates within that identified regime; no formal-findings requirement follows. |
| Thomas | Affirm this application of the actual Hale rule. | Joined Lopez's enforceable-boundary rule and the unanimous Hale and Rybar commerce portions. The valid interstate-stock regime supplies the necessary relation; mere national marketability would not. |
| Ginsburg | Affirm on the common ground. | Joined Hale Part I and Rybar Part I. Absence of an individual crossing does not defeat class regulation; no empirical stock-provenance finding or crime-cost rationale is necessary. |
| Breyer | Affirm on the common ground. | Joined Hale Part I and Rybar Part I. Predictive and design latitude supports including retained converted stock after the regime connection is identified, without substituting aggregate magnitude for that connection. |

### Alternative paths and scope

The strongest reversal path preserves Hale but distinguishes possession produced by wholly local conversion from a weapon acquired in a sale, arguing that no transfer element or admission establishes this conviction's connection to the market. Its strongest counterargument is the regime's direct concern with additions to prohibited stock: exempting retention of locally converted completed weapons would leave the very additional stock the prohibition controls available for concealment and circulation. All eight reject making a demonstrated prior sale a universal constitutional prerequisite. That condition would narrow the existing class-and-regime rule into a transaction rule it expressly declined to adopt.

The strongest objection to affirmance is that treating every marketable object's possession as necessary to a national market would erase Lopez's boundary. The adopted ground answers it through the particular enacted transfer/stock restriction and material impairment from excluding this completed prohibited stock. It approves no free-standing possession ban justified only by marketability, remote movement, gun crime, fear, insurance, or productivity. It does not decide every conversion-parts, readily-restorable, or wear-induced application of the incorporated definition. The statute's government-related exception and its separate exception for lawful transfer or possession of a machinegun lawfully possessed before May 19, 1986, remain intact; manufacture before that date alone is not enough, and no exception is established here.

Lopez is applied, not overruled: connection precedes magnitude and courts may not insert a missing offense element. Hale supplies the controlling anti-evasion/material-impairment rule; Rybar supplies a recent application, not an additional interstate-crossing or proved-sale element. Parker's cross-border support obligation is a distinct mechanism and supplies no substitute machinegun rule. Wickard and Perez retain their economic-class scope without performing the dispositive work here.

**Remedy and limits:** Affirmance concerns only the preserved Commerce challenge to Count One. It reinstates no dismissed transfer count, decides no Second Amendment claim, and reopens none of the ungranted plea-agreement, double-jeopardy, or sentencing issues. No evidentiary remand is needed merely to obtain original documents or find an interstate crossing the governing ground does not require. No separate writing is necessary to preserve a material Associate disagreement.

**Source/cutoff:** February 14, 1998. The frozen packet's published lower-opinion recitations supply indictment, conditional plea, conversion, test firing, and the limits of the sale narrative; no additional plea admission, interstate movement, finding, original brief, or later action is asserted. Ready for assembly.

The approved October 21 supplement supports the protest-letter dismissal, protected-litigation retaliation, Mt. ## Adaptive audit annex

## 2. Johnson v. Rodriguez — February 17, 1998

### Threshold and component results

The reviewed matter is an official-capacity action for prospective relief after a bench trial. It is not a damages-immunity appeal. The Fifth Circuit's remand does not create a §1257 state-court-finality problem; the authorized review is of a federal court of appeals under §1254. No affirmative untimeliness or unexhausted statutory-vehicle fact is supplied. The frozen packet's introductory reference to an unspecified statutory vehicle obstacle identifies no concrete obstacle and supplies no dismissal premise.

All eight Associates adopt the following component positions, subject to the particular scope qualifications in the individual table:

| Component | Reconciled disposition | Sufficient ground and remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Initial-parole procedural liberty / protest-file process | Affirm rejection of the asserted entitlement and the resulting process demand. | Texas's eligibility limitations, guidelines, file requirements, and mandatory consideration of a victim-impact statement do not require release once specified facts are found. Sandin's actual substantive-constraint rule does not turn procedures alone into a release entitlement. Young protects freedom already conferred; Johnson remains in ordinary sentence-authorized confinement. |
| Protest-letter equal protection | Affirm dismissal with prejudice of this distinct claim. | Even assuming the treatment of prisoners receiving protest letters supplies a comparison, receiving relevant information, permitting victim participation, protecting sources from reprisal, and avoiding a full adversarial parole hearing are rational purposes. The trial court's unreliable-information concern does not establish purposeful unconstitutional differential treatment or justify excluding every protest statement. No universal rule that an equal-protection class must predate government action is adopted. |
| Writ-writer retaliation | Preserve the remand, but vacate the appellate directions insofar as they categorically exclude all secondary assistance/other independent protected petition activity or put the entire same-decision burden on the claimant. | Identify protected activity and an adverse action actually attributable to retaliation. Under Crawford-El and Mt. Healthy, Johnson must prove protected conduct and its substantial or motivating role; officials then may prove by a preponderance that the same action would have occurred without it. A conceivable lawful parole reason is not that proof. No ultimate retaliation finding follows. |
| Writ-writer equal protection | Preserve this separate claim on remand under corrected protection and causation premises. | The claimant must establish relevant similarly situated treatment and purposeful discriminatory effect; general references to litigation or historical bias by another agency do not suffice. A penalty for independently protected litigation is not justified merely by calling all litigiousness unreformed behavior. No strict-scrutiny rule or liability finding is adopted. |
| Standing, attributable practice, common relief | Preserve remand for actual findings; do not reinstate the statewide decree. | Johnson must establish his own redressable injury and the prospective basis for relief. The challenged systemic practice must be attributable to the defendant Board actors; old Ruiz findings about other agencies and subjective perceptions do not establish it. Class relief requires supported common injury and must fit the proven violation. |
| Attorney fees | Affirm vacatur of the dependent award. | The reversed trial decree no longer sustains that award. Any later prevailing-party entitlement depends on the lawful judgment eventually entered; no amount or permanent fee disability is decided. |

### Justice-specific commitments and join tests

| Justice | Adopted position and personal authority | Material limits, broader or narrower position |
|---|---|---|
| Stevens | Adopts each component above. Joined Breyer's Sandin controlling constraint rule; joined Kennedy's effective-assistance rule in Lewis; joined Crawford-El's ordinary proof and same-decision rules and Souter's Umbehr and Valot rights-penalty holdings. | Would preserve genuinely established findings and allow supported common evidence; his narrower-remand position in Lewis counsels against discarding such evidence. Here the missing protected-activity, causal, representative-injury, and Board-attribution findings independently prevent restoring the decree. Will not require a lost lawsuit as proof of injury from a retaliatory parole denial. |
| O'Connor | Adopts each component on the bounded grounds stated. Joined Young's existing-liberty distinction, Kennedy's controlling Lewis access and remedial portions, Souter's Umbehr, and unanimous Crawford-El. | Protected prison litigation must be identified, and the access-specific necessary-assistance issue remains distinct from a free-standing right to act as another prisoner's lawyer. Her Valot public-employment position does not establish a public-concern prerequisite for a prisoner's own nonfrivolous court challenge. No new general petition rule is needed. |
| Scalia | Adopts each component and the limited corrective remand. Joined Young, Lewis's controlling hindrance and remedial portions, and Crawford-El. | No general state-created parole entitlement or universal protection for all jailhouse work. Would require actual predicate, attribution, and injury findings and retain valid prison restrictions. Applying Crawford-El's actual defense allocation does not adopt Umbehr's distinct extension to contractors, from which he dissented. |
| Kennedy | Adopts each component, including careful separation of retaliation injury from a Bounds access claim. Authored Lewis's effective-access, qualifying-hindrance, and remedial rules; joined Young, Crawford-El, Umbehr, and Valot. | His Lewis rule does not make every retained-right claim depend on an unsuccessful filing or categorically terminate assistance protection after filing. Adequate alternative legal assistance and legitimate penological restrictions remain material. No statewide remedy without supported reach. |
| Souter | Adopts each component. Joined Breyer's Sandin rule and Kennedy's Lewis effective-assistance/remedial portions; authored Umbehr and Valot; joined Crawford-El. | Absence of a parole entitlement is no license to retaliate against a separately protected invocation. Independent communication or petition predicates must be examined rather than rejected through access-specific language. This preserves a remand, not a finding that every assistance activity is protected. |
| Thomas | Adopts each component on the stated narrow scope. Joined Young, Lewis's controlling access and remedial rules, and Crawford-El. | Insists on identified nonfrivolous protected activity, actual adverse effect, and supported causal responsibility. No generic right to be a jailhouse lawyer, heightened statewide-resource entitlement, or automatic relief from loss of parole. Neither his contractor dissent nor employee public-concern position displaces the controlling prison-access rule or Crawford-El. |
| Ginsburg | Adopts each component. Joined Sandin's constraint rule, Lewis's effective arrangements and remedial fit, Crawford-El, Umbehr, and Valot. | Protection of completed lawful petitioning remains distinct from proof that access was prevented. No categorical rejection of otherwise necessary help for a prisoner unable to proceed without it. Comparative proof may be nonstatistical; missing statistics alone do not defeat every possible retaliation case. |
| Breyer | Adopts each component. Authored Sandin's actual entitlement rule and Young's existing-liberty rule; joined Lewis's effective arrangements/remedial portions, Crawford-El, Umbehr, and Valot. | The whole Texas scheme leaves initial release discretionary despite meaningful eligibility limits. Practical common evidence may prove injury, but the supplied findings do not establish the needed plaintiff-specific and Board-specific connections. The remand should resolve those actual matters without imposing a new evidence code. |

### Operative rules, alternatives, and preserved distinctions

**Parole and protest letters.** The strongest broader-remand argument invokes Sandin's rejection of mechanical mandatory-word analysis and the substantive public-safety/eligibility criteria in Texas law. The answer is substantive, not verbal: those conditions limit when release may be granted, but do not materially restrict the Board's authority to deny the initial release sought here. No release has already conferred the community liberty protected in Young. Conversely, the absence of entitlement does not decide whether a distinct First Amendment penalty is permissible. All eight will join the disposition only with that separation.

The protest-letter judgment can rest on ordinary rational review without deciding that no classification could ever exist absent an antecedent group. The strongest objection is the trial finding that some statements are inaccurate, vindictive, or unrelated to its preferred criteria. That finding does not establish that every receipt or consideration of a statement lacks a legitimate relation to parole judgment, or that the broad exclusion remedy follows. The decision does not approve knowing official falsification, racial discrimination, punishment of protected litigation, use of a judicially invalidated conviction in defiance of a binding order, or every conceivable use of an individual false statement. Those distinct claims are not established by this protest-letter class judgment.

Article 42.18 §8(f)(2)'s mandatory victim-related notice, permission for written and oral participation, absence of a numerical ceiling on written speakers, and mandatory consideration of the victim-impact statement are separate commands and permissions. Section 8(e)'s file-inclusion requirements do not command reliance on every included allegation. Section 18(a)'s confidentiality is not a finding that all claimed accuracy defects are immaterial under every possible constitutional theory.

**Retaliation and access.** A State's discretion to deny a benefit does not permit denial because of independently protected conduct. The claimant must identify that conduct, show the challenged adverse act and its substantial or motivating connection, and establish the ordinary injury and attribution predicates. The officials may then prove by a preponderance that the same action would have occurred without the protected conduct. A potentially sufficient lawful parole reason, without an actual counterfactual showing, does not satisfy that defense. Ordinary competent direct and circumstantial evidence remain available; no clear-and-convincing or categorical direct-evidence requirement is added.

Lewis governs a claim that inadequate assistance actually or imminently obstructed a qualifying nonfrivolous legal claim. It does not require a prisoner alleging retaliation for a completed protected filing to prove that the filing failed. Johnson v. Avery and Wolff preserve the significance of assistance when necessary to recipients' meaningful court access; the State may supply effective alternative arrangements and enforce valid penological restrictions. No free-standing entitlement to serve as another prisoner's chosen lawyer follows. The remand must distinguish that necessary-access possibility, Johnson's own nonfrivolous filings, frivolous activity, and any separately grounded communication or petition theory actually within the case. It may not declare that every assistance activity is protected or that all assistance is constitutionally irrelevant.

The strongest complete-affirmance path relies on the Fifth Circuit's correct rejection of blanket protection and on genuinely inadequate trial findings. It fails only where its directions import a categorical Lewis restriction or displace Mt. Healthy's burden allocation. Those legal corrections do not erase the legitimate need for further findings. The strongest reinstatement path relies on repeated mentions of litigation and the trial court's general chilling finding. It fails because the record does not connect identified protected activity and attributable Board retaliation to Johnson's parole decision, establish the necessary representative injury, or support the decree's statewide scope. Missing source originals prove no default; the published appellate account itself identifies the missing findings that make remand, rather than appellate merits factfinding, appropriate.

**Equality and remedy.** The rights-dependent writ-writer equality theory remains distinct from protest-letter process and independent ordinary-equality theories. Comparable treatment and purposeful adverse effect must be established under their proper legal predicates; no universal statistical-proof requirement is imposed. Likewise, a conceivably rational ordinary classification is not an actual Mt. Healthy defense to a proved protected-right penalty. Class certification does not establish standing or a statewide wrong. Systemic relief requires a supported common practice and affected group and must fit the proved violation, respecting valid security interests and applicable prospective-relief law. The holding adopts neither a universal Monell requirement for every state-officer injunction nor an entitlement to purge all litigation references. Here the challenged Board-wide practice itself requires proof of Board attribution.

**Mandate:** Affirm the protest-letter dismissal and fee vacatur; vacate only the legally incompatible writ-writer directions; remand the retaliation and writ-writer equality claims for reconsideration consistently with the stated rules and actual record. The existing directive for further proceedings survives otherwise. No parole, release, fresh trial, compulsory discovery, liability, damages, fee award, or statewide injunction is ordered. Unappealed ex post facto, tentative-parole-month/progress, nonresident-furlough, and corporate-entity immunity dispositions stay closed. No personal qualified-immunity ruling is made.

**Source/cutoff:** February 17, 1998. Source report and full published lower opinion, 110 F.3d 299, including footnotes, support the posture and unresolved findings. OCR §636(e) and April 80 are corrected only by the authorized source report to §636(c) and April 30, 1996. Original parole files, trial transcript, and pleadings are not claimed read. The appellate generalization that many prisoners' suits lack merit is not a finding that all of Johnson's pertinent conduct is unprotected. Ready for assembly.

## Adaptive audit annex

## 4. Newsweek, Inc. v. Florida Department of Revenue — February 23, 1998

**Result:** Each of the eight Associates supports granting certiorari, vacating the Florida judgment, and remanding for Newsweek to use the clearly held-out postpayment procedure to adjudicate its claim. The prepayment alternative does not justify withholding that opportunity. No fixed refund is ordered. This corrects the provisional formal label of reversal while preserving its substantive remand and all remedy limits.

| Justice | Reconciled commitment and date-eligible personal basis |
|---|---|
| Stevens | Vacate and remand on Reich, which he joined, and Fulton's unanimous remedial distinction. His joins in Camps Newfound's remedial portion support leaving lawful state correction choices open. |
| O'Connor | Vacate and remand under her unanimous Reich opinion. A clearly offered postpayment route cannot be replaced after payment with an unpursued prepayment alternative. |
| Scalia | Vacate and remand under his joins in Reich and Fulton's remedial portion. The case requires no acceptance of a new substantive tax rule or of Camps Newfound's separate invalidity theory. |
| Kennedy | Vacate and remand under Reich, Fulton, and his join in Camps Newfound's open-remedy instruction. Preserve ordinary conditions announced before payment and actual payment/amount proof. |
| Souter | Vacate and remand under Reich and Fulton and the remedial holding he joined in Camps Newfound. Adequate correction does not automatically select a particular refund calculation. |
| Thomas | Vacate and remand under Reich and his unanimous Fulton opinion. Prior availability of §72.011 does not answer the independent postpayment-reliance ground. |
| Ginsburg | Vacate and remand under Reich and Fulton, which she joined. Her disagreement with Camps Newfound's distinct Commerce disposition does not supply a reason to depart from this existing due-process rule. |
| Breyer | Vacate and remand under Reich and Fulton and his controlling Camps Newfound remedial portion. Federal remedial adequacy and permissible state choices remain separate. |

**Operative holding:** When a State has clearly held out a postpayment procedure for recovering unconstitutionally collected taxes, it may not deny that promised opportunity after payment solely because the taxpayer could have pursued an adequate prepayment challenge. Florida's longstanding §215.26 route, used here for the 1988–1990 payments, supplies that premise; §72.011's deposit, bond, or approved-alternative routes do not retrospectively displace it. Relief remains subject to lawful reasonable preannounced conditions and ordinary proof of payment and amount.

**Alternative-path test:** Florida's strongest defense is that McKesson's compelled-payment premise is absent because prepayment review was meaningful. Even assuming that premise for Florida, Reich independently protects the clearly available postpayment route, including voluntary payments. Conversely, the argument that invalidity requires an immediate refund of every dollar goes beyond Reich, Fulton, and Camps Newfound, which preserve constitutionally adequate lawful correction choices. The bounded vacate-and-remand path answers both without declaring §72.011 inadequate or deciding a condition-default not found in the source.

**Treatment and remedy:** Reich is applied directly; McKesson's particular backward-looking duty is distinguished from the independent no-withdrawal rule rather than enlarged into an automatic-refund requirement. Fulton and Camps Newfound preserve lawful remedial choices. Florida's prior Magazine Publishers invalidity ruling is the established predicate, not a new substantive First Amendment adjudication by this Court. Vacate and remand for a clear and certain postpayment opportunity; no dollar amount, interest, new assessment, fee, exemption, general government-estoppel rule, or reopening of final judgments follows. No separate Associate writing is needed on these bounded grounds.

**Source/cutoff:** February 23, 1998. The neutral control extraction establishes 1988–1990 payments, §215.26 invocation, the Florida judgments, the longstanding refund route, and the alternative §72.011 procedures. No independent timeliness or refund-condition default is established. Original return, refund application, and pleadings are not claimed read, and no default is inferred from that research limit. Ready for assembly.

assignment_statements.text:
**Case and dockets:** Rivet v. Regions Bank of Louisiana, No. 96-1971.
**Event and date:** Plenary merits decision, 1998-02-24; argued 1998-01-21; October Term 1997, chunk 4.
**Result:** Reversed and remanded 9–0; all dependent federal merits judgments vacated; action must return to state court.
**Version / lineage:** Original decision.

## Event validation and entering law

Research cutoff: 1998-02-24. The seated Court consists of Chief Justice Stone-Zsela and Justices Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer. All nine participate at submission and decision; no case-specific recusal or nonparticipation is established. The full Court has a quorum and five votes supply an ordinary merits majority. The public Holdings, Precedent Treatment and Law After Decision blocks below also constitute this Record's controlling-holding section, copied without substantive alteration for downstream use. ## Source separation and status

The reconciliation SHA-256 is c0286755f26108b21beabd48a024394fa5b9da0bedf43d1a0a6cfbd6c3096d71. Independent modeling and historical reconciliation occurred in separate scoped contexts. This assembly performs final compatibility; it claims no blindness to Stone or the comparator. The frozen commitments are unchanged. Local checks cover identity, component disposition/ground/remedy, exact Stone joins, all eight Associate commitments, participation, vote arithmetic, form-first choice, actual-table assignment recount where applicable, and the eleven-block projection. Workspace integration, generated Render Input identity and the repository term checker remain pending root integration; this Record does not claim those unperformed checks passed. The assembly validation receipt records the completed mechanical checks. Public separate positions below are the complete material noncontrolling continuity for this event; no other new roster, allotment or institutional change occurs.

## Lawful channel, Stone and chronology

Review proceeds by certiorari under section 1254(1) from the Fifth Circuit, following January 21, 1998 argument. Original removal jurisdiction is the threshold question under sections 1331 and 1441. The October 21 approved Stone position reverses the Fifth Circuit, vacates all dependent federal merits judgments and requires state-court remand. His legal ground distinguishes a federal defense from an exclusive federal cause supplied by complete statutory preemption. The opinion's treatment of Moitie and the earlier jurisdiction cases supports that ground without adding an alternative Stone rule or altering his remedy. He joins the complete opinion; no fallback is used. The Browns' independently reasoned merits judgment falls because it shares the missing jurisdictional foundation, not because its substantive ground was found erroneous.

All eight Associates retain their frozen full agreement. No majority or new rationale is manufactured by converting judgment-only agreement into a join. Regions is an uncoordinated same-day event and supplies no new entering-law premise; it enters only the required authorship count. Earlier Johnson and Newsweek concern distinct claims and do not change this jurisdictional rule or record.

## Form and sequential assignment

One signed plenary jurisdiction-and-remedy opinion was selected on legal grounds in the form-first receipt. Before assignment the actual current Record opinion tables were copied again, including Regions, into the [Rivet evidence](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK4_RIVET_ASSIGNMENT_EVIDENCE.json), and recounted in the [count receipt](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK4_RIVET_COUNT_RECEIPT.json). Counts: Stone-Zsela 3; Stevens 4; O'Connor 5; Scalia 3; Kennedy 4; Souter 4; Thomas 4; Ginsburg 4; Breyer 4. Last counted event: Regions, February 24, Breyer, first in same-day alphabetical order; 35 prior signed plenary leads. Every Justice joins every proposition and is eligible. Minimum 3; pool Stone-Zsela, Stevens, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer. O'Connor is fully eligible but outside the pool.

Stone assigns to Scalia for fit and the lower-count preference. This opinion's work is to insist on the pleaded statutory jurisdictional source, distinguish a claim's legal character from a defense defeating it, and remove dependent merits judgments without deciding the defense. Scalia's actual Peacock and City of Chicago joins support each boundary; his Allentown treatment of the difference between the actual governing standard and a substituted premise demonstrates the same disciplined explanatory task. Thomas is the strongest alternative through authorship of Peacock and Chicago, but their settled rules can be applied equally faithfully without a new accommodation, and Scalia's count is lower, three to four. Stone's approved jurisdiction/merits separation fits the work at the same low count but supplies no unique formulation or coalition advantage over Scalia. No historical Rivet authorship or separate part determines the choice. Scalia writes the whole lead and receives one count.

The full historical Supreme Court comparator supports the eight preserved Associate positions. There is no material historical departure. The lower court relied on complete claim preclusion, not a holding that a statute completely preempted these Louisiana causes of action. The source correction is retained. No later preclusion development or actual mortgage-merits finding is used.

## Adaptive audit annex

## 6. Rivet v. Regions Bank of Louisiana — February 24, 1998

**Result:** All eight Associates would reverse the Fifth Circuit's jurisdictional judgment, vacate the dependent district-court merits judgments, and remand with instructions to return the action to Louisiana state court. The prior bankruptcy orders may support a preclusion defense; that defense is not original federal-question jurisdiction.

| Justice | Reconciled commitment and personal date-eligible basis |
|---|---|
| Stevens | Reverse and require state-court remand. Joined Caterpillar's insistence on actual jurisdiction and Richards's separate binding-authority rule; his City of Chicago dissent resists deriving jurisdiction from general federal concerns in a state proceeding. His broader enforcement position in Peacock does not convert a defense in this independent state action into §1331 jurisdiction. |
| O'Connor | Reverse and remand on the common rule. Authored Caterpillar's actual-jurisdiction limit and Matsushita's distinction between recognition and adjudicatory power; joined Peacock. Prior judgment recognition may be strong without generating removal power. |
| Scalia | Reverse and remand. Joined Peacock, Caterpillar, and Thomas's City of Chicago federal-anchor holding. The statutes and actual cause of action, not anticipated federal defenses, supply jurisdiction. |
| Kennedy | Reverse and remand. Joined Peacock, Caterpillar, Matsushita, and City of Chicago. His Baker concurrence's narrower recognition reasoning leaves unchanged the distinction between a judgment's lawful effect and an independent jurisdictional source. |
| Souter | Reverse and remand. Joined Peacock, Caterpillar, and City of Chicago; joined Baker's bounded recognition/execution rule. Enforcing lawful preclusion does not require treating every precluded claim as a federal claim. |
| Thomas | Reverse and remand. Authored Peacock's independent-authority rule and City of Chicago's holding that substantial federal claims on the complaint's face supplied the removal anchor there. Here that anchor is absent. |
| Ginsburg | Reverse and remand. Joined Peacock and Caterpillar; her City of Chicago dissent preserves careful statutory jurisdiction boundaries and her Baker join separates recognition from new duties in another forum. No need to resolve the actual force of the mortgage cancellation. |
| Breyer | Reverse and remand. Joined Peacock, Caterpillar, Matsushita, and City of Chicago. Finality and efficient adjudication cannot cure an absent original jurisdictional basis, unlike actual pretrial diversity in Caterpillar. |

**Operative holding:** Under §§1331 and 1441, the assertion that a prior federal judgment precludes a complaint presenting only state-law claims is a defense and does not transform that complaint into one arising under federal law. Complete statutory preemption is different: it concerns whether federal law supplies the claim's controlling legal character, not whether an earlier federal judgment defeats an otherwise state-law claim. An artful-pleading label or the asserted completeness of claim preclusion cannot supply the missing original jurisdiction.

**Application and alternatives:** The mortgage holders seek recognition/enforcement of Louisiana mortgage rights or alternatively damages under Louisiana law; the parties are Louisiana parties. The respondents invoke the bankruptcy orders to defeat those rights. Even if the orders conclusively extinguished them, that would answer a defense, not establish removal jurisdiction. The strongest contrary path reads Moitie footnote 2 as allowing removal whenever federal claim preclusion wholly bars a later state claim. The eight decline that extension: relabeling an essentially federal claim and asserting preclusion of an independent state claim are different. Moitie's ordinary preclusion rule is preserved; the footnote supplies no general exception for this defense. No finding that these petitioners prevail on the mortgage or may disregard the bankruptcy orders follows.

Peacock supplies the need for independent statutory authority in a later action and preserves lawful enforcement within its proper sphere. Chicago had substantial federal claims on the face of the complaints; it cannot supply supplemental jurisdiction here with no original federal anchor. Caterpillar preserves a completed judgment only when actual original jurisdiction exists by trial and judgment; all-Louisiana citizenship and a federal defense provide no such cure. Matsushita, Richards, and Baker retain their own recognition, binding-authority, and execution limits; none makes recognition law a universal removal grant.

**Mandate and scope:** Reverse and remand for the district court to vacate the merits judgments entered without the asserted jurisdiction and return the whole action to state court. The Browns' summary judgment rested on failure to state a claim, not the Banks/FSA preclusion ground; it nevertheless lacks an independent federal jurisdictional foundation and is not affirmed on its merits. The Court resolves no mortgage priority, cancellation efficacy, bankruptcy-order validity, actual preclusion element, damages entitlement, or substantive claim against any respondent. Otherwise available enforcement proceedings retain their actual authority and prerequisites; no new injunction or collateral attack on the bankruptcy orders is authorized. No separate Associate writing is needed on this bounded jurisdictional ground.

**Source/cutoff:** February 24, 1998. The neutral additional extraction supports the 1983/1984 mortgages, June/August 1986 orders, 1993 transfer, December 29, 1994 state suit, common Louisiana parties, exclusive Louisiana pleading, and distinct Browns judgment. It does not supply the complete original instruments or a new jurisdictional theory. No missing original is treated as a litigant failure; the supported complaint/jurisdiction posture suffices for the limited removal decision. Ready for assembly.

assignment_statements.text: **Controlling explanation:** The sentence limits federal credit-union membership, not merely the labels assigned to each component group. The plural groups permits multiple groups sharing a common occupational bond; it does not make a succession of unrelated bonds sufficient. The agency’s reading retains internal group and service-area conditions, but those are different from the connection Congress imposed on the membership. The parallel geographic alternative supports that reading. NCUA’s concession that the geographic groups must occupy the same defined community is an attributed argument, not a separate holding on geographic charters. MCI requires enforcement of an enacted boundary before deference. NationsBank permits reasonable financial classifications within an authorized domain and does not permit removal of its boundary. General rulemaking authority, serviceability and administrative efficiency cannot replace the required bond. A changed interpretation is not invalid merely because it changed. The decision imposes no single-employer requirement and does not determine the full breadth of a genuine occupation or association, geographic charters, or individual membership-retention rights.

assignment_statements.text:
**Case and dockets:** Kawaauhau v. Geiger, No. 97-115.
**Event and date:** Plenary merits decision, 1998-03-03; October Term 1997; chunk 5.
**Result:** Affirmed, 9–0; the negligence-or-recklessness malpractice debt is dischargeable under §523(a)(6).
**Version / lineage:** Original decision.

## Decision kernel

The accepted malpractice judgment follows treatment of Margaret Kawaauhau’s infected foot: Geiger chose oral rather than more effective intravenous penicillin, later canceled a proposed specialist transfer and stopped antibiotics because he believed the infection had subsided. Her condition deteriorated and her leg was amputated below the knee. The approximately $355,000 judgment includes Margaret’s injury damages and Solomon’s consortium and emotional-distress damages. Geiger lacked malpractice insurance. The bankruptcy court’s willful-and-malicious characterization is a disputed federal legal conclusion, not a finding that he intended injury. The preserved statutory question is dispositive; this Court neither retries malpractice nor finds subjective intent. The certiorari merits stage ends in affirmance.

**Participation and channel:** All nine seated Justices participated at argument or submission and decision; no nonparticipation is established. A quorum is present and five votes suffice for each Court disposition. Review proceeds through the stated lawful channel.

**Entering law:** The exact reading copy is entering-law/CHUNK5/01_geiger.md, supplemented by the Geiger-only clean neutral addition. Field, effective November 28, 1995, preserves the independent federal predicates of a discharge exception and ordinary proof by a preponderance; In re Cohen, effective June 30, 1997, addresses the extent of debt after a qualifying fraud predicate, not this injury predicate. Tinker, McIntyre and Davis remain available at their actual scopes. The contextual criminal-scienter cases supply no civil criminal-proof or lenity rule. The independent March 3 decisions share a pre-day merits baseline; Bogan enters the assignment count only, and neither Bogan, Lexecon nor Spencer supplies merits law here.

### Stone position and final compatibility

The approved current Section II directs affirmance and reaches only negligent or reckless malpractice under the willfulness requirement. It requires deliberate or intentional injury and reserves substantial certainty, the independent meaning of malicious, other independently pleaded exceptions and proved injury-directed intent. Every holding below remains within that core. Stone joins the whole opinion; there is no fallback, additional ground, separate remedial choice or separate writing. No later current-term premise changes his approved question or remedy.

### Opinion structure and component coalitions

One signed opinion, with all nine joining the injury-intent rule, its bounded application and the identified precedent treatment. The judgment and rationale coalitions coincide. No fractured-decision analysis or invented circulation exchange is needed.

## Controlling holdings

### Deliberate injury is required; a deliberate act causing negligent or reckless harm is insufficient

**Holding and operative rule:** Section 523(a)(6) requires a deliberate or intentional injury, in addition to the separately stated malicious character; intentionally doing an act that negligently or recklessly causes injury does not satisfy willfulness. This malpractice debt, established on negligence or recklessness rather than injury-directed intent, is therefore dischargeable under that paragraph.

**Authority:** Ginsburg’s opinion of the Court, joined in full by all eight other Justices identified in Opinion Topology, directly controls the rule, application and stated limits.

**Controlling explanation:** The statutory modifier describes injury. Moving it to the treatment decision would make many voluntary acts producing negligent harm sufficient and deprive the injury requirement of independent work. The medical choices here were deliberate, but that does not establish deliberate injury. The exceptionally deficient standard of care found below establishes malpractice; calling it willful and malicious does not answer the federal question.

Tinker involved an intentional invasion of a legally protected right, and McIntyre involved deliberate unauthorized appropriation of property. Neither requires personal hostility, but neither makes a voluntary act alone enough. Tinker itself distinguished negligent driving from intentionally running over a victim. To the extent its broader language is read to include merely reckless injury under the present statute, that reading is rejected. Davis confirms that even conversion liability does not automatically establish willful and malicious injury. Field likewise keeps a federal discharge predicate distinct from a state tort label.

The creditors’ cumulative account of inferior treatment, canceled transfer and discontinued antibiotics establishes the gravity of the alleged wrong, but supplies no additional finding of intended injury. Nor does uninsured practice authorize a judicially created exception. Congress fixes the exceptions. The Court reserves whether subjective knowledge of substantial certainty suffices, the independent meaning of malicious, any other independently pleaded discharge exception and the treatment of proved injury-directed harm. No categorical exemption for medical debts or new criminal-law proof requirement follows.

## Precedent and resulting law

- Tinker v. Colwell, 193 U.S. 473, retains its intentional-invasion holding and rejection of a personal-hostility requirement; a reading that makes merely reckless injury sufficient under §523(a)(6) is rejected.
- McIntyre v. Kavanaugh, 242 U.S. 138, is distinguished as deliberate appropriation; it does not make all conversions or negligent professional acts nondischargeable, and its old-Act imputation question is not decided.
- Davis v. Aetna Acceptance Co., 293 U.S. 328, is applied to preserve the distinction between tort liability and willful and malicious injury.
- Field v. Mans is applied for the independent federal discharge predicates; its actual-fraud reliance rule is unchanged. In re Cohen’s debt-extent rule remains distinct because a qualifying injury predicate must first exist here.

From March 3, 1998, §523(a)(6) excludes debts for negligently or recklessly inflicted injury from its willfulness category even when the underlying act was intentional. Actual deliberate injury presents a different question. The independent malicious requirement, substantial certainty, other discharge exceptions and state-law liability retain their separate roles.

## Continuity

The discharge rule and its reservations are those in the controlling holding. No separate noncontrolling position is published. No institutional, roster or companion dependency changes. The jury’s malpractice finding and damages calculation are not revisited; dischargeability is the issue resolved. This review supplies no further pending Court matter.

## Sources and validation

Neutral authority: freeze/OT_1997CHUNK5_NEUTRAL_A.md, Geiger section only, plus research/chunk5_control/GEIGER_CLEAN_NEUTRAL_ADDITION.md. The clean addition supplies full pre-event Tinker/McIntyre/Davis verification and the correct statutory text. Source-control SOURCE_READ_RECEIPT.md records the complete official 523 U.S.57–64 read, including footnotes; assembly relies on that receipt for full-original coverage and on the released objective recitations, not on unrecovered briefs. The primary citation supports historical facts; the present opinion and assignment are independently constituted. No unknown document establishes default.

**Research cutoff:** 1998-03-03. No later event is a merits premise.

**Preservation and validation:** This new Record is durably written at `terms/OT1997/records/kawaauhau_v_geiger_merits_1998-03-03.md`. Assembly checks confirm the four-label opening, the eleven ordered public blocks, identical internal/public holding text, the stated component arithmetic, and assignment-pool compliance where applicable. The full term validation is a separate integration check; no claim that it has already run is made here. No unresolved substantive source blocker remains for these bounded holdings.

## Adaptive audit annex

### Frozen commitments and historical reconciliation

The authoritative [A1 reconciled freeze](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK5_A1_RECONCILED.md), including K1–K3, the adversarial alternatives, every individual row and its final-release addendum, is incorporated at that exact case scope. The individual frozen rows are copied below.

| Justice | Result and sufficient ground | Own date-eligible authority, scope and join boundaries |
|---|---|---|
| Stevens | Affirm under K1–K3 | His unanimous Field Part I join requires the actual federal exception predicates rather than a state tort label. His Ratzlaf and X-Citement Video joins treat the statutory mental-state term as an operative, contextual requirement. Here willfulness modifies injury; exceptional malpractice alone is inadequate. Joins the common-law distinctions and narrowly rejects a reckless-disregard use of Tinker. Does not import criminal lenity or demand personal hostility. |
| O'Connor | Affirm under K1–K3 | Her Field Parts I–II joins distinguish liability, federal discharge predicates and correct-standard application. Her narrow Staples concurrence join and X-Citement Video join preserve the exact object of a statutory mental-state requirement. Injury-intent is missing from the negligence/recklessness ground accepted below; treatment choice does not supply it. Joins K1–K3 without deciding substantial certainty or a complete malice rule. |
| Scalia | Affirm under K1–K3 | His Field Part I join accepts established legal terminology while his different application position preserves disposition on sufficient existing findings. His Ratzlaf and Staples joins give the chosen mental-state language its operative object. The words willful and malicious injury cannot be reduced to voluntary act plus resulting harm. Text and Tinker/McIntyre/Davis distinctions suffice; does not make legislative reports a necessary ground or decide later intentional-injury cases. |
| Kennedy | Affirm under K1–K3 | His Field join preserves federal predicates distinct from state liability; his Ratzlaf, Staples and X-Citement Video joins support context-specific mental-state construction. A physician's purposeful treatment act does not itself prove purposeful injury. Joins the bounded Tinker treatment, Davis distinction and affirmance; no categorical immunity for medical debts or general malice definition. |
| Souter | Affirm under K1–K3 | His Field opinion supplies the direct method of construing statutory legal terms against their common-law setting while keeping the distinct exception requirements separate. Tinker and McIntyre involved intentional invasions; Davis refused automatic classification from conversion liability. Joins the text-based injury requirement and affirmance on the supplied negligence/recklessness issue, leaving subjective certainty and other exceptions open. |
| Thomas | Affirm under K1–K3 | His Field join and Staples opinion support honoring the actual culpability object rather than collapsing it into intentional conduct generally. His unanimous In re Cohen opinion, identified in the slice's register, likewise requires a qualifying federal predicate before debt consequences follow. No such §523(a)(6) injury predicate follows from this malpractice judgment. Joins the text and precedent distinction; legislative purpose cannot enlarge the enacted exception. |
| Ginsburg | Affirm under K1–K3 | Her Ratzlaf opinion and X-Citement Video opinion use context to identify the element to which culpability attaches; her Field join preserves independent bankruptcy predicates. Here the enacted object is injury, not simply a deliberate medical choice. Joins the historical intentional-invasion distinction and affirmance, without importing her criminal cases' proof burdens or residual lenity holdings into bankruptcy. |
| Breyer | Affirm under K1–K3 | His Field Part I join accepts the federal common-law predicate, and his separate application position favors applying the correct rule to sufficient accepted findings rather than automatic remand. His X-Citement Video join supports a mental-state construction suited to the statutory object. Treating all voluntary negligent acts as willful injury would erase the limitation's function; the text and prior distinctions support affirmance on this defined record. No new subjective finding or complete malice test. |

Reconciliation retains all eight commitments: the unchanged injury-intent, intentional-invasion and malpractice premises support the historical unanimous alignment. No material departure is found. Historical authorship supplies no assignment entitlement. The live assembly received the A1 freeze before its Stone section. The distinct early exposure concerning later A cases supplies no Geiger premise.

### Form, assignment and final joins

**Form fixed first:** freeze/OT_1997CHUNK5_A1_FORM_FIRST.md fixes one signed plenary opinion and its complete common propositions before counting.

**Assignment authority:** Chief Justice Stone-Zsela assigns from the unanimous affirmance coalition.

**Before-assignment counts:** Stone-Zsela 4; Stevens 5; O'Connor 5; Scalia 4; Kennedy 4; Souter 5; Thomas 5; Ginsburg 5; Breyer 4.

**Last counted event:** Bogan v. Scott-Harris; No. 96-1569..

**Eligible authors:** Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer.

**Balance pool:** Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer.

**Author selected:** Ginsburg. Ginsburg’s actual Ratzlaf, X-Citement Video and current-term Bates opinions coordinate the precise object of a mental-state term with the statutory work that term performs. That is the central task here: explaining injury-directed intent without importing a criminal burden or converting every deliberate treatment choice into intentional harm. Scalia is the strongest lower-count alternative through his Ratzlaf and Staples joins and textual work; he can carry the rule, but Ginsburg’s demonstrated authored coordination of the specific culpability/object distinction gives a concrete fit advantage. Stone’s Fink bankruptcy work and approved injury/act distinction also make him eligible at four; neither requires self-assignment or supplies a closer demonstrated mental-state analysis. Ginsburg remains within the minimum-plus-one pool. No accommodation or historical-author preference supplies the selection.

**Recount evidence:** `freeze/OT_1997CHUNK5_GEIGER_ASSIGNMENT_EVIDENCE.json` records the actual preceding public opinion topologies and their individual classifications. Separate writings add no count. This signed plenary merits lead counts once for its author.

Final compatibility: Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer retain K1–K3 in full; Stone joins their common rule and application on his approved injury-intent ground. Keeping substantial certainty and malice open answers the scope limits already recorded. No commitment changes and no new circulation history is posited.

assignment_statements.text: Lexecon Inc. v. Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach, No. 96-1482. Plenary merits decision, March 3, 1998; argued November 10, 1997. On writ of certiorari under 28 U.S.C. §1254(1) to the Ninth Circuit. The question is whether an MDL transferee court may use 28 U.S.C. §1404(a) to assign a transferred action to itself for trial despite §1407(a)’s remand command. Lexecon’s Illinois diversity tort action was transferred to Arizona for coordinated pretrial proceedings. The Arizona court entered pretrial dispositions, denied requests to suggest remand and retained the defamation claim for a defense trial judgment; the Ninth Circuit sustained the self-transfer. Lexecon preserved the objection through remand requests, mandamus and direct appeal.

The following bounded extract reproduces the final reconciliation’s individual commitments, grounds, alternatives and limits. Statements describing an earlier context’s source access refer to that completed stage. It does not itself assign authors or supersede the final topology above. Authority: `freeze/OT_1997CHUNK4_B_RECONCILED.md`, SHA-256 `952fa983417f39a31d6c4b5f569bbecde603d77886a14553a66c4c544ec9e1ab`; the independent commitment freeze remains unchanged.

Section 1407 authorizes common-fact coordination for pretrial proceedings. Unless the action has previously terminated, the Panel must remand it to the original district at or before those proceedings end; the Panel may separate and remand particular claims earlier. Section 1404(a)'s general permission to transfer to another district or division where the action might have been brought does not authorize the §1407 transferee to assign the continuing action to itself for trial and defeat that remand. Changing the asserted venue basis does not terminate an action. The fact that the command expressly addresses the Panel does not let a transferee court prevent its performance. Subsection (f) authorizes only rules consistent with Acts of Congress; the cited practice cannot overcome the statute. Subsection (h)'s specific Clayton Act trial-transfer permission does not confer that power in this tort action.

**Version / lineage:** Original decision.

## Decision kernel

The warrant’s validity is undisputed. A reliable informant reported a person believed to be Alan Shelby, a dangerous escaped prisoner, at Ramirez’s house; an agent saw a similar-looking man there. Officers also received information about weapons in the garage. Approximately 45 officers executed the warrant early in the morning. A loudspeaker announcement accompanied the breaking of one garage window and the pointing of a firearm through it to prevent access to the reported weapons. Ramirez believed burglars were entering, fired into the garage ceiling, and surrendered after police identification and returned fire. He waived Miranda rights and admitted firearm possession and felon status; a later warrant recovered the guns. Shelby was absent. The District Court found insufficient exigency for destructive entry under both the Constitution and §3109; the Ninth Circuit affirmed on its heightened standard. The Court resolves only the supplied entry and damage questions, not the legality of every subsequent act or an independent suppression claim.

**Participation and channel:** All nine seated Justices participated at argument or submission and decision; no nonparticipation is established. A quorum is present and five votes suffice for each Court disposition. Review proceeds through the stated lawful channel.

**Entering law:** The exact slice is entering-law/CHUNK5/02_ramirez.md plus the Aponte Matos public projection in CURRENT_PUBLIC_LAW_A.md. Wilson’s May 22, 1995 announcement principle and Richards’s April 28, 1997 particularized reasonable-suspicion standard govern. The Announcement before dwelling entry register’s present operation is Richards, April 28, 1997; its fact/legal review allocation is preserved but not newly decided. Aponte Matos concerns qualified immunity and 1993 notice, not a direct suppression defense. The independent §3109 text and Miller/Sabbath authorities are supplied by the final clean Ramirez freeze. Geiger changes bankruptcy law only and does not alter these questions. No March 9 decision enters the merits baseline.

### Stone position and final compatibility

The approved current Section II expressly reaches the Constitution and §3109, directs reversal and remand, supports traditional exigency exceptions and particularized danger, and independently assesses the nature and extent of property damage. Its concrete application finds the single window proportionate to the reported escapee/weapons danger. Stone joins all three holdings and the bounded remedy. The statutory holding applies his approved traditional-exception ground to danger; reserving applications to other exigencies repudiates no approved position. The opinion adds no new review-method ground or suppression-causation rule. No fallback, separate opinion, expanded force approval or remedy for materially different destruction is supplied. The exact case-only mechanical copy is runtime/OT_1997CHUNK5_RAMIREZ_STONE.md.

### Opinion structure and component coalitions

One signed plenary opinion. All nine support the same reversal and remand and fully join the separate constitutional rule, execution application and statutory construction. Section 3109 is not collapsed into the Constitution, and reasonable surprise is not treated as authority for unlimited destruction. No fractured-rationale or changed-commitment question arises.

## Controlling holdings

**Common authority:** Breyer’s opinion of the Court is joined in full by all eight other Justices identified in Opinion Topology. That direct unanimous coalition controls each holding and its limits; no combination of separate rationales is necessary.

### I. Property damage does not raise the announcement threshold

**Holding and operative rule:** Damage during warrant execution does not categorically require a greater exigency than particularized reasonable suspicion that ordinary announcement would be dangerous or futile, or would inhibit effective investigation, including through destruction of evidence. The facts supporting that exception must be known when the challenged force begins, and the means and extent of any destruction remain independently subject to Fourth Amendment reasonableness.

**Controlling explanation:** Wilson makes the common-law announcement protection part of constitutional reasonableness while preserving supported exceptions. Richards requires particular facts and rational inferences rather than an offense category, unsupported hunch or a no-knock label on a warrant. Breaking property does not change that announcement inquiry into a separate higher tier. The contrary rule correctly recognizes that destruction aggravates an intrusion, but addresses that concern in the wrong place. Whether the particular destructive act is reasonable remains a separate question; justified surprise does not authorize needless or disproportionate damage. The Court adopts no universal waiting period and revisits no disputed standard-of-review rule.

### II. The contemporaneous danger and limited damage justified this execution

**Holding and operative rule:** The reliable report of a dangerous escapee, corroborating observation and location-specific information about garage weapons supplied reasonable suspicion that ordinary announcement would create danger. Breaking one garage window to control access to those weapons, with a firearm directed through the opening for that purpose, was reasonable on this record; the justification permits neither gratuitous destruction nor any amount of damage merely because announcement may be excused.

**Controlling explanation:** Richards requires circumstances known before force. The informant’s report was partly corroborated by the agent’s observation, and the reported weapons gave the officers a concrete reason to prevent a rush into the garage. The limited window break addressed that identified danger. The number of officers outside did not eliminate a possible armed person’s access to weapons inside. Their security purpose is supported by those facts; purpose alone would not suffice. Ramirez’s later shot supplies no retrospective justification, and the later failure to find Shelby does not erase the information reasonably available beforehand. The Court decides the challenged entry and window damage, not every subsequent act. Gratuitous, punitive, disproportionate or objective-unrelated destruction receives no approval, and the remedy for materially different damage remains open.

### III. Section 3109 preserves a supported common-law danger exception

**Holding and operative rule:** Section 3109 ordinarily permits breaking to execute a search warrant after notice of authority and purpose and refused admission, and separately permits breaking when necessary to liberate the officer or someone assisting execution. Its codification of the common-law announcement rule also preserves a danger exception satisfied by particularized reasonable suspicion that following the ordinary process would expose officers or occupants to danger; the pre-entry escapee and garage-weapons information satisfies that exception here.

**Controlling explanation:** Simultaneous announcement and breaking do not establish prior refused admission. Nor does this record establish an officer or assistant needing liberation. The entry instead rests on the incorporated common-law danger qualification. Miller identifies the common-law source of the statutory protection but reserved a general exigency question. Sabbath treats opening an unlocked door as breaking and, in its discussion of common-law exceptions, supplies direct interpretive support without having held that every asserted danger suffices. Indeed, its unsupported danger claim failed. The Court now adopts the danger construction for the concrete supported circumstances here; it does not attribute that holding to those earlier reservations.

The statutory protection carries its traditional safety qualification, rather than automatically acquiring every constitutional exception. Wilson’s common-law account and Richards’s particularized standard guide this bounded construction. The express liberation alternative concerns freeing an impeded officer or helper and remains distinct. Because breaking already includes entry without physical damage, the statute creates no greater announcement threshold merely because property is damaged. No statutory rule for every possible futility, escape or evidence-destruction situation is necessary. Both asserted grounds for suppression fail, so the Court need not decide attenuation, independent source, inevitable discovery or the exclusionary consequence of an established violation.

## Precedent and resulting law

- Wilson v. Arkansas is applied for the common-law announcement protection and supported exceptions; it does not constitutionalize every federal statutory detail.
- Richards v. Wisconsin is applied for particularized reasonable suspicion and contemporaneous justification; its announcement quantum is not increased because damage occurs, and its separate review-method holding is unchanged.
- Miller v. United States, 357 U.S. 301, supplies the statutory common-law background. Its reservation of a general exigency exception is respected rather than described as an earlier holding.
- Sabbath v. United States, 391 U.S. 585, retains its rule that opening a closed unlocked door is breaking and its rejection of unsupported danger. Its common-law discussion supports the danger qualification adopted here; physical damage creates no new announcement tier.
- Aponte Matos v. Toledo Dávila retains its separate conduct-date qualified-immunity scope and supplies no direct suppression immunity here.

The constitutional announcement inquiry retains Richards’s particularized reasonable-suspicion standard when execution damages property, while the destructive means receive independent reasonableness review. Section 3109 separately incorporates the supported common-law danger exception applied here. Neither the validity of a warrant nor the availability of an announcement exception authorizes unreasonable damage. No suppression-causation doctrine or rule for materially different destruction is resolved.

## Continuity

No separate noncontrolling position is published. Scalia’s earlier withheld Richards review-method join is undisturbed because the present opinion does not newly adopt or extend that rule. The constitutional and statutory execution rules govern prospectively from this event; the prosecution returns for further proceedings under the bounded reversal. ## Event, jurisdiction, participation and entering law

The full Court acts under Rules 39.8, 38 and 33.1 on the present fee motion and separately on prospective filing control. ## Controlling holdings

### I. The present fee motion

**Holding and operative rule:** Rule 39.8 permits, but does not require, denial of financial leave when the particular submission is frivolous or malicious, even if the applicant cannot prepay. The Court exercises that discretion here because the present petition supplies no arguable route through the independent state-action, conspiracy and judicial-immunity obstacles to the federal action; it allows payment of the Rule 38 fee and submission in Rule 33.1 form by March 30, 1998, without deciding certiorari.

**Authority:** Part I of the per curiam opinion, joined by O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer; seven Justices adopt this rule, application and limited filing opportunity. Stevens and Stone-Zsela would grant the motion as a permissible discretionary choice.

**Controlling explanation:** The Court examines the grounds Glendora actually presents. She alleges false service, lack of personal jurisdiction and denial of a hearing to challenge service, and contests the appellate financial warning and clerk-signed order. Those allegations are not rejected as false. They nevertheless supply no developed arguable challenge connecting the service dispute to the independent immunity, state-action and conspiracy grounds defeating this federal action. A clerk's signature and the challenged panel composition do not themselves establish a federal defect. The Court does not confuse its own appellate jurisdiction with the District Court's inability to review a state judgment.

Martin requires particular-paper assessment and preserves a discretionary denial where an independent obstacle receives no arguable answer. Demos and Anderson permit an arguable access allegation to clear the fee threshold without proving entitlement to relief, but do not make the allegation's label conclusive. Arteaga applies the same distinction between considering an actual procedural explanation and finding an arguable route through the operative obstacle. The lower court's characterization, financial warning and unsuccessful filing history do not substitute for this examination. Financial denial is not a finding of wealth, dishonesty or default, and it decides neither the alleged misconduct nor any claim's ultimate merits. Payment and proper form permit ordinary processing, not a promised grant of review.

### II. The proposed restriction on future noncriminal petitions

**Holding and operative rule:** A prospective fee-and-form restriction requires demonstrated applicant-specific abuse, a supported fit to the future category restricted, and support for the inadequacy of individual-paper treatment. The present record does not establish those predicates for Glendora's unidentified future noncriminal certiorari petitions, so the Court imposes no new restriction.

**Authority:** Part II of the per curiam opinion, joined by all nine Justices: Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer.

**Controlling explanation:** Martin, Day, Sassower, Anderson, Brown and Arteaga require an independent justification for future restraints. The present petition's deficiencies and the lower-court warning do not demonstrate repeated applicant-specific abuse fitted to all future noncriminal petitions, or why individual treatment is inadequate. A count of unsuccessful filings cannot establish the content of unidentified future papers. Keeping paid and criminal routes available would narrow the proposed condition but would not supply the missing justification. This refusal creates no numerical threshold, universal prior-warning requirement, duty to exhaust every conceivable lesser measure, or categorical prohibition on adequately supported restrictions. Targeted controls remain available on their own demonstrated predicates.
