assignment_statements.text:
**Case and dockets:** United States v. Hinds; Fourth Circuit No. 97-4030; Middle District of North Carolina No. CR-96-148. No separate Supreme Court docket supplied.
**Event and date:** Plenary merits decision, 1998-04-06; October Term 1997, chunk 6.
**Result:** Fourth Circuit affirmance vacated and remanded, 8–1, for bounded review of the existing trial record. Stone-Zsela would reverse and direct acquittal on the §844(i) count.
**Version / lineage:** Original decision.

## Event, authority and entering law

The authorized lower-court addition supplies ordinary review under 28 U.S.C. §1254(1) and the April 6, 1998 decisional anchor. It supplies no recovered historical Supreme Court grant, docket or argument date. The event follows full merits consideration under the approved review setting, not summary disposition. No separate argument or submission date is established. The Fourth Circuit's October 15, 1997 affirmance is the judgment under review, not the later district report at 74 F. Supp. 2d 637. Before this event the federal conviction was affirmed; after it the appellate affirmance is vacated and existing-record review remains below.

All nine sitting Justices participate at merits submission and decision: Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer. No recusal or nonparticipation is established. Nine supply a quorum and five would supply a judgment or proposition majority. Stevens is the senior Associate. No roster, allotment or institutional-practice change occurs.

The [validated neutral packet](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK6_B_VALIDATED_NEUTRAL.md), its [receipt](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK6_B_NEUTRAL_VALIDATION.md), and the [entering-law slice](../entering-law/OT_1997CHUNK6_B.md) supply the record and effective law. Section 844(i)'s property-use condition, Russell's rental holding, Bailey/Robinson's independently required conditions and bounded remand, Burks and the current Jacobson insufficiency remedy control the reached questions. Lopez's connection-before-magnitude standard, its later current applications and Agostini's modified Lemon inquiry remain governing background, not newly decided constitutional grounds.

The six exact intervening Public Projections in [the reading directory](../entering-law/chunk6_intervening_public/) were read: Almendarez-Torres (March 24), Woodard (March 25), and Feltner, Texas, Scheffer and U.S. Shoe (March 31). None changes the statutory-use condition or makes Stone's present proof, remedy or constitutional reach position inapplicable. Almendarez-Torres concerns classification of a different recidivist fact, not omission of this conceded offense element; Feltner changes no criminal jury waiver. Woodard and Scheffer create no general remand entitlement. Texas's unripe hypothetical intervention differs from this entered conviction. U.S. Shoe supplies no new Commerce standard. Kirk and Robinson have actually been decided in the entering-law slice; their regime and operating-business holdings do not displace §844(i)'s independent property-use text. The March 31 events supply no substantive interdependence among themselves.

The statutory issue is reached first. The second granted question, Congress's outer Commerce authority over this application, is not reached. The Court leaves the Establishment objection unnecessary to its judgment. No §247 charge, penalty amendment, other offense, independent sentence or release claim is decided. No precise offense date, unreported commercial activity, origin of every purchase or complete trial-evidence finding is invented.

## Stone's fixed position and exact final joins

The full [scoped approved supplement](../runtime/CHUNK6_SCOPED/united_states_v_hinds_STONE.md), including its October 23 revision, was read after the [reconciled freeze](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK6_HINDS_RECONCILED.md). Stone's fixed core is reversal on §844(i)'s active-commercial-use requirement, immediate vacatur and acquittal for the proof's present insufficiency, no decision of the second granted question, and rejection of the Establishment objection through Agostini's established-permissible-relationship route. The acquittal is not made conditional on a further proof inquiry. The substantive distinction from the Associates remains intact.

His partial joins are confined to the exact propositions the Opinion Topology states. He does not join the complete property-function formulation's refusal to make commercial use a prerequisite, the existing-record remand or a conditional substitute for immediate acquittal. His Burks join adopts only the already approved insufficiency/acquittal proposition. He adds no proof standard, burden, qualification, new evidentiary opportunity or constitutional holding to his approved position. His separate writing preserves his legal work: distinct statutory rule, disagreement on present sufficiency and remedy, and the reason the rejected religious objection supplies neither avoidance context nor an alternative basis for reversal. No fallback is used. No clerical correction, substantive narrowing or alternative discretion branch is invoked.

The source limitation about an unreproduced full trial record qualifies the Court's account; it is not attributed to Stone as withdrawal of his authorized sufficiency conclusion, and it is not a finding of litigant default. His position describes the legal consequence he draws from the approved record account. The eight Associates decline that ultimate inference and order only lawful existing-record review.

## Public judgment and opinions

**Vacated and remanded, 8–1.**

**Supporting:** Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer.
**Opposing:** Stone-Zsela.

The Fourth Circuit's affirmance is vacated. That court must apply the statutory construction to the existing trial record and determine the lawful disposition of the §844(i) conviction. No additional evidence or new trial is authorized. An actual finding of evidentiary insufficiency requires reversal for entry of acquittal; any supported adequate use basis and necessary, properly presented constitutional question must be addressed under current law. The Court does not itself direct acquittal, release, a substitute conviction or resentencing. Stone-Zsela would instead reverse and direct vacatur of the conviction and immediate entry of acquittal on this count.

| Writing | Author | Joined by | Relationship to judgment | Scope joined |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opinion of the Court | Stevens | O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer | Vacates the Fourth Circuit's affirmance and remands | Part I's complete property-function construction and application; Part II's existing-record mandate and constitutional nonreach |
| Same opinion, partial joins | Stevens | Stone-Zsela | Agrees that the affirmance cannot stand; opposes the Court's operative remand | Part I only as to independent work for the property-use element, insufficiency of owner relationships by themselves, and absence of a religious exemption; Part II only as to the independent Burks rule that evidentiary insufficiency requires acquittal and bars retrial to repair proof |
| Concurrence in part and dissent from the judgment and remand | Stone-Zsela | No other Justice | Would reverse and direct vacatur of the §844(i) conviction and entry of acquittal on that count | Active-commercial-use construction; present insufficiency and immediate acquittal; separate Agostini-based reason for rejecting the Establishment objection as a construction aid or alternative ground |

## Controlling holdings

### I. The damaged property's use must connect it to commerce

**Holding and operative rule:** Section 844(i) requires a connection between the function performed by the damaged property and interstate or foreign commerce, or an activity affecting that commerce. The owner's national affiliation, purchases, an employee's out-of-state insurance and recurring payments do not establish the element merely by existing; their relation to the property's use must be established, without making religious or nonprofit ownership an exclusion or profit-making, rental, sales or an exclusively business purpose a universal prerequisite.

**Authority:** Stevens's Opinion of the Court, joined in full by O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer, supplies eight direct joins to the complete construction and its application. Stone-Zsela joins only the propositions that the property-use element has independent work, that the owner's identified economic relationships by themselves do not establish it, and that religious identity creates no exemption. He does not join the complete formulation's rejection of an exclusively commercial-use requirement; his active-commercial-use construction is stated separately.

**Controlling explanation:** The Court holds that the statute asks what the damaged property was used to do and how that function connects with commerce. Russell sustains coverage of a rented apartment building because renting the premises placed the property itself in the rental market. Its broad account of statutory coverage does not erase the enacted use limitation, and its rental example does not establish an exclusive class of covered property. The words extending coverage to an activity affecting commerce retain both their breadth and their connection to the property's use.

The Fourth Circuit correctly recited the property-use element. Its application nevertheless treated the congregation's economic relationships as sufficient without establishing their relation to the function of the damaged premises. Annual transfers through a national denomination are actual movements of money, and thus the Government's strongest asserted connection. But the existence of those transfers does not itself explain the building's qualifying function. The same distinction applies to the employees, employee insurance, utilities, religious materials and other purchases. The Court neither doubts those reported relationships nor assumes every purchase came from outside the State.

Bailey/Robinson supplies the statutory distinction between required conduct and another related condition: satisfying one does not dispense with the other. Its firearm-use rule is not transplanted into this statute. Section 844(i)'s own use language does the work here. The Court adds no interstate-travel requirement, no profit-making condition and no requirement that this individual fire substantially affect the national economy. The panel's stated rationale cannot sustain its affirmance; the complete trial proof must be considered under the correct construction. No constitutional ruling or categorical exclusion of religious premises follows.

**Precedent treatment:** Russell remains controlling for actual rental use and is applied without turning that example into exclusive coverage. Bailey/Robinson is applied at the distinction between separately required statutory predicates, not as an independent definition of property use.

### II. The appellate judgment is vacated for review of the existing trial record

**Holding and operative rule:** The Fourth Circuit's affirmance is vacated, and that court must apply the property-use construction to the complete existing trial record and determine the lawful disposition of the §844(i) conviction; this mandate authorizes neither additional evidence nor a new trial. If the existing evidence fails to establish the required use connection, the court must reverse for entry of acquittal, because evidentiary insufficiency cannot be repaired through another trial; if existing proof supports a legally adequate use finding, the court must identify that basis and address any necessary, properly presented constitutional question under current law.

**Authority:** Part II of Stevens's opinion has the same eight Associate joins. Stone-Zsela joins the independent Burks proposition that actual evidentiary insufficiency requires acquittal and bars a second opportunity to supply missing proof, but rejects this judgment and remand: he finds the proof insufficient now and would direct acquittal immediately. No condition of the Court's further-review mandate is attributed to his position.

**Controlling explanation:** The Court corrects the legal application supporting the appellate affirmance. It does not decide that the complete trial record contains no other evidence relevant to the damaged building's function. Those are different determinations. The lower court must examine existing proof under the rule announced here; it may not treat this remand as permission to build a new prosecution case.

Burks requires acquittal after a determination that the prosecution's evidence is legally insufficient. Jacobson applies that consequence and forbids another opportunity to supply missing proof. Those authorities control if the existing record establishes only institutional relationships without the necessary property-use connection. Conversely, a legally adequate use finding cannot be assumed merely because the conviction once stood. Any such basis must actually be supported, and any necessary preserved constitutional question must then be addressed.

Bailey/Robinson illustrates the distinction between correcting an erroneous statutory premise and deciding every remaining lawful basis or remedial predicate. Its separate carrying branch creates no alternative element here. The remand determines neither acquittal nor retrial in advance, and orders no release, substitute §247 conviction, amended penalty or independent sentencing disposition. The Court reaches neither Congress's outer Commerce Clause authority nor the Establishment Clause objection.

**Precedent treatment:** Burks and Jacobson preserve the mandatory acquittal consequence of actual insufficiency. Bailey/Robinson supplies a bounded remedial analogy, without a new carrying theory, new evidence or an automatic retrial rule.

## Precedent treatment and resulting law

- **Russell v. United States, 471 U.S. 858 (1985):** Applied at its actual rental-use holding and retained statutory use limitation. Rental remains sufficient in its established setting, without becoming an exclusive class or establishing automatic church coverage.
- **Bailey v. United States; Robinson v. United States, December 6, 1995:** Applied at the separation of independently enacted conditions and used as a bounded remedial analogy. Its active-firearm-use and carrying rules are not imported into §844(i).
- **Burks v. United States, 437 U.S. 1 (1978), and Jacobson v. United States, April 6, 1992:** Applied to require acquittal after actual evidentiary insufficiency and prohibit another trial to repair missing proof.
- **United States v. Lopez and its current applications, including United States v. Robinson, March 23, 1998:** Preserved without a new constitutional application. Statutory jurisdictional words remain no automatic constitutional safe harbor, and each statute retains its actual elements.
- **Agostini v. Felton and Tanford v. Brand:** Unchanged. The Court does not decide the Establishment objection; Stone-Zsela's separate application of Agostini and Everson establishes no additional Court holding.

Section 844(i)'s property-use element requires the relationship between the function of the damaged premises and commerce or a commerce-affecting activity. The owner's economic relationships alone do not suffice. Religious and nonprofit premises receive neither categorical exclusion nor automatic coverage. Existing-record review must distinguish a legally adequate use basis from insufficient proof; the latter requires acquittal and cannot support another evidentiary opportunity. The Court changes no Commerce Clause or Establishment Clause standard and decides no §247, penalty-amendment or other-charge question. Stone-Zsela's exclusive active-commercial-use formulation, immediate-acquittal application and separate Establishment explanation do not bind lower courts.

## Continuity and published separate position

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and dissenting from the judgment and remand.** The enacted use requirement demands active employment of the building itself in commercial activity. The congregation's purchases, utilities, insurance, staff, donations, mail and national affiliation are economic relationships; they do not transform premises devoted to worship into property actively employed in commerce. The national denomination's annual redistribution of funds to missionaries, seminaries, institutions of higher education and other programs is the Government's strongest argument, but it still describes what the congregation paid and gave in support of worship, rather than commercial use of this building. Russell's rented premises illustrate the distinction because the property itself operated in the rental market. The Fourth Circuit stated the use element but answered it through the congregation's economic connections. Stone-Zsela considers the Government's proof insufficient now. Under Burks and Jacobson he would reverse, direct vacatur of the conviction and entry of acquittal, and deny another trial to repair that proof.

Lopez supplies avoidance context, not a constitutional judgment. Its connection-before-magnitude sequence raises doubt about a reading that reaches every building through an owner's insurance, purchases, payroll or gifts and their downstream economic consequences. Avoidance is available because Congress enacted a use limitation to construe; it permits no inserted element. The existence of jurisdictional wording is not itself a constitutional safe harbor. Lopez preserves genuine economic-class analysis under Wickard and Perez and does not require a substantial effect from each individual act. Stone-Zsela leaves Hinds's particular substantial-effect contention and the outer Commerce question undecided. Hale, Rybar and Kirk's protection of a valid machinegun regime does not dispense with this statute's different property-use element. Robinson's direct interference with operating business assets likewise supplies no all-purchases rule. Robertson's commercial enterprise transactions and Allied-Bruce's broader transaction-involving-commerce language do not replace §844(i)'s property-use text.

This is no religious exemption. Stone-Zsela reserves the reach of the statute over religious property itself used for a commercial enterprise, rental activity, substantial commercial leasing or materially mixed commercial use. He decides no particular application within those categories, no authority under another federal statute, including FACE's unchallenged worship branches, and no reach of differently worded statutes such as the Hobbs Act. Ordinary state arson law and independently valid federal charges retain their own elements and limits.

He separately rejects the Establishment objection as a reason to construe the statute differently for religious property or as an alternative ground for reversal. Under Lemon as Agostini modified it, a specific prohibition or distinct doctrine resolves conduct it covers; an established permissible relationship defeats a covered claim; otherwise a legally sufficient unresolved claim proceeds through attribution and function. Purpose, effects and entanglement are evidence within that inquiry, not independent or fallback prongs. The governmental act here is prosecution of an alleged arsonist, and its function is ordinary property protection. Everson's established relationship of general public-welfare services, including ordinary police and fire protection, resolves the objection, provided the criminal statute validly applies.

The prosecution organizes no worship, prescribes no religious profession or observance, adopts no doctrine, solicits no religious adherence, governs no theology, confers no religiously allocated civil authority and finances no devotion. Examining a congregation's operations to determine an offense element is not regulation of its religious teaching or governance. Tanford involved the government's own organized commencement worship and therefore a different function. Facial neutrality and the beneficiary's identity are contextual evidence, not independently decisive grounds. Stone-Zsela reaches neither the residual route nor an accommodation, funding, legislative-prayer or ceremonial question; free exercise and religious autonomy retain their distinct sources and burdens. His answer creates no rule permitting every governmental benefit to religion, supplies neither statutory coverage nor an enumerated power, and does not ground his reversal. The second granted question remains unreached; insofar as the Establishment objection falls outside the grant, this discussion states only his reason for declining to rely on it. No other Justice joins this separate explanation.

The mandate authorizes no new evidence or retrial and assumes no alternative basis for affirmance. No release or independently chosen sentencing order is entered. #### I. Intentional force and threats directed at the provision of reproductive services fall within the established commerce connection

**Holding and operative rule.** Congress may apply §248(a)(1) to intentional force and true threats directed at preventing a person from providing reproductive-health services because that conduct operates directly on access to an actual interstate service market. The connection is the conduct's object and operation, not generalized costs of violence; neither the offender nor each affected clinic must separately cross a state line.

**Authority.** Kennedy's Part I, joined by all eight other Justices, controls the Commerce question and the affirmance on that ground.

**Controlling explanation.** The Court holds that American Life League supplies the governing connection. Its sustained class is direct interference with provision or receipt of reproductive-health services in an interstate market. Lopez requires a constitutionally identifiable connection before aggregate effects can justify federal regulation; it does not permit Congress to turn every local crime into a national economic problem. Bird's bottle attack and threat to kill a physician entering the clinic to provide services directly obstruct that service activity. The absence of proof that this physician, clinic staff, patients or supplies crossed a state line does not sever the conduct from the class American Life League sustained. FACE's conduct and purpose elements do the necessary work; the Court inserts no omitted jurisdictional element. Hinds concerns a different statute's property-use requirement and supplies no such element here. The defense's local-violence objection thus fails on the access-directed mechanism, without a new theory based on fear, healthcare expense or lost productivity. This holding does not federalize ordinary assault, trespass, protest or disturbance merely because it occurs near a medical facility, and does not decide materially different mixed-purpose conduct. Alternative §5 authority and reconsideration of protected-choice law are unnecessary.

#### II. The supervision component requires a determination of a continuing controversy before its merits

**Holding and operative rule.** When the actual operation of a challenged supervision condition and any continuing redressable consequence remain unresolved, a live challenge to the conviction does not itself establish jurisdiction to decide that condition's merits. The appellate disposition affirming the condition is vacated, and the matter returns through the Fifth Circuit to determine that threshold on the actual supervision record; the district condition itself is neither vacated nor rewritten by this decision.

**Authority.** Kennedy's Part II-A, joined by all eight other Justices, controls the continuing-controversy requirement and the limited appellate vacatur. Part II-B's precise remand and reservation of the condition's merits is joined by Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer: eight Justices including the author. Stone-Zsela does not join Part II-B and would add mandatory replacement if the dispute is live.

**Controlling explanation.** The Court holds that jurisdiction must attach to the relief actually sought. Spencer distinguishes a live custody-related injury from presumed consequences after the particular restraint ends. That requirement informs this distinct sentencing component without making every direct-sentencing appeal equivalent to Spencer's revocation case. The sentencing date and stated terms do not establish commencement, operative delay, tolling, expiration or an actual present burden. Nor does a live conviction challenge establish them. Section 2106 authorizes appropriate further proceedings but creates no merits jurisdiction. A bounded remand allows the lower courts to use judicial materials that establish status, without demanding duplicative production. Only proceedings supported by the actual jurisdictional finding may follow. If the dispute is live, the condition remains subject to §3583(d)'s reasonable relationship to the relevant sentencing purposes, no greater liberty deprivation than reasonably necessary, and pertinent policy-statement requirements. If it is moot, no condition-merits ruling may issue; the proper mootness disposition and any equitable treatment of the lower judgment depend on actual timing and circumstances. The Court presently requires neither retention nor narrowing nor removal of the condition. Past violence supports a serious protective interest but cannot resolve unknown jurisdiction or predetermine the appropriate breadth. No general resentencing or extension of supervision follows.

The separate lower-court familial-classification, overbreadth, vagueness and written-judgment-label disputes are not independently within the questions adjudicated here. Their lower dispositions are not new holdings of this Court.

- American Life League v. Reno, decided November 13, 1995, is applied to the service-directed force and threats. Its conduct, purpose and speech-protection boundaries remain intact; this decision adds no new facial speech ruling.
- United States v. Lopez, decided April 26, 1995, is applied to require an identifiable commerce connection before aggregation. Direct interference with the established service market supplies that connection here.
- United States v. Hinds, decided April 6, 1998, is distinguished: its statutory property-use inquiry does not insert an element into FACE or change the Commerce rule.
- Spencer v. Kemna, decided March 3, 1998, supplies the actual-continuing-injury principle. Its revocation holding is not enlarged into a categorical rule about every direct sentencing challenge or a finding that this condition has expired.
- Madsen v. Women's Health Center, Inc., 512 U.S. 753 (1994), and Schenck v. Pro-Choice Network, decided February 19, 1997, remain relevant fit analogies if condition merits become reachable. Their injunction rules establish neither an automatic criminal-supervision test nor a universal permissible distance here.

There is direct nine/eight-Justice authority at the stated scopes and no Marks issue. The Commerce decision applies the existing rule; supervision remains open below only under the bounded mandate. The published separate position is retained verbatim in the public handoff at its noncontrolling scope. The restitution, assessment and other unreviewed matters are unaffected by this judgment. This direct-criminal Commerce and Article III disposition changes no material premise of A-732's emergency first-habeas application or Carriger's independent capital gateway dispute; no new conditional supervision reasoning enters their law. Parent term-wide dependency review remains separate.

## Adaptive audit annex

The final component commitments and Justice-specific grounds below are script-copied from the immutable [reconciled handoff](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK6_RESUMED_RECONCILED.md). The [fresh commitments](../freeze/OT_1997CHUNK6_RESUMED_COMMITMENTS.md) preserve each conditional retention/correction comparison; these are not adopted present holdings.

## 3. United States v. Bird — April 13, 1998

**Conviction:** Each Associate supports affirming the conviction against the reviewed Commerce challenge. American Life League's service-directed class and direct interference with the interstate reproductive-services market control the bottle attack and threat against a physician entering to provide services. The connection is that conduct's object and operation, not generalized national crime costs. The holding requires no separate crossing or clinic-specific interstate proof and permits no invented offense element. Hinds's different property-use language supplies none.

**Scope:** Each Associate leaves unnecessary §5 and protected-choice questions undecided, and does not independently adjudicate the lower-only familial-classification, overbreadth, vagueness or judgment-label claims. The separate supervision authorization includes that question alone. Prior FACE holdings remain law without turning unaccepted claims into new holdings.

**Supervision:** Each Associate supports vacatur only of the Fifth Circuit judgment insofar as it affirms the 1,000-foot, all-clinics special condition, followed by a bounded jurisdictional remand through that court. The district condition itself is not vacated or rewritten. Actual commencement, operative delay or tolling, expiration, current restraint and redressable consequences remain unresolved. The remand determines continuing controversy and permits only the lawful proceedings that follow. All eight also accept the narrower alternative of retaining the component for a bounded inquiry into actual Article III facts, with disposition and merits reserved. That recorded alternative is available for final compatibility without inventing a new commitment.

| Associate | Final positions and personal source-based limit |
|---|---|
| Stevens | Conviction affirmance, scope nonreach and limited supervision jurisdictional remand. His American Life League join supplies the market rule. His Madsen and Caspari scope positions support nonreach. His Spencer dissent concerned an identified reputational injury, absent here; it supplies no universal continuing-injury presumption. His individualized remedial approach remains a conditional consideration if merits become reachable. |
| O'Connor | Same three dispositions. Her American Life League join reconciles her Lopez connection requirement with this service market. Her authored Madsen fit analysis matters only after jurisdiction and does not automatically transplant an injunction test or numerical radius to criminal supervision. |
| Scalia | Same three dispositions. His American Life League join preserves the federal boundary without a personal-crossing requirement. His Spencer join requires an actual surviving interest. His stricter Madsen dissent remains a conditional speech-restraint concern, not a present invalidity vote. |
| Kennedy | Same three dispositions. His authored American Life League supplies both the direct market rule and reservation of alternative §5 power. His Spencer join requires the threshold inquiry; his Madsen dissent does not equate criminal supervision with that injunction. |
| Souter | Same three dispositions. His American Life League and question-scope joins support the conviction and nonreach. His Spencer join, rather than Stevens's particular disagreement there, governs continuing injury. His Madsen joins preserve a relationship between misconduct and territorial burden if merits are reached. |
| Thomas | Same three dispositions. His Lopez and American Life League joins recognize this particular connection, and his Spencer join forecloses presumed continuing injury. His Madsen dissent permits no ideological exclusion and supplies no present condition merits vote. |
| Ginsburg | Same three dispositions. Her American Life League, scope and Spencer joins support the present grounds. Her Madsen/Schenck joins require fitted protection and retained lawful advocacy, conditionally and without inserting a civil-injunction distance rule into §3583(d). |
| Breyer | Same three dispositions. His American Life League join supplies the connection; his authored Spencer requires an actual surviving controversy and the stated exception predicates. His Schenck join informs conditional fit. No pre-appointment Madsen vote is attributed to him. |

**Threshold and conditional limits:** The conviction's live controversy does not automatically preserve every separate sentence condition; sentencing-date arithmetic establishes neither expiration nor mootness. Section 2106 permits appropriate further proceedings but creates no merits jurisdiction. A genuine judicial status question, not a local archive gap, supplies the inquiry's purpose. Existing judicial material resolving status should be used without duplicative production. Any eventual mootness disposition or equitable vacatur depends on actual timing and circumstances; no automatic consequence is fixed here.

If live, §3583(d)'s reasonable relationship, no-greater-than-reasonably-necessary liberty restriction and policy-statement requirements retain independent force. Prevention based on violence, trespass and resistance to restrictions is the strongest retention ground; all-clinics reach and burdens on lawful access, movement and advocacy are the strongest correction concerns. Madsen and Schenck provide fit analogies, not an automatic governing test, universal radius or least-restrictive-means requirement. Every Associate's conditional retention/correction comparison and narrower statutory path in the frozen handoff is retained. None is a present merits vote or a mandate to retain, narrow or remove the condition.

No conviction retrial, acquittal, restitution or assessment change, general resentencing, extension of supervision, stay, release or new exclusion follows. The lower appellate merits affirmance does not establish a Supreme Court historical alignment against this limited jurisdictional response. No commitment changes on reconciliation.

No historical Supreme Court merits lineup exists for this lower-court addition. The lower appellate affirmance supplies no Supreme Court authorship or Justice-specific departure. Final votes and scope remain those frozen above, with Stone added only at assembly.

assignment_statements.text:
**Case and dockets:** Breard related applications: Republic of Paraguay et al. v. Gilmore, No. 97-1390 (A-738); In re Breard, No. 97-8660 (A-767); Republic of Paraguay et al. v. Gilmore, No. 125 Original (A-771).
**Event and date:** Compound Court order deciding three emergency applications, 1998-04-14; October Term 1997, chunk 6.
**Result:** A-738 denied 9–0; A-767 denied 6–3; A-771 denied 5–4. No execution restraint. A-732 and all accompanying petitions/leave proceedings remain undecided.
**Version / lineage:** Original decision.

## Event, chronology and scope

Breard v. Greene and related applications: Republic of Paraguay et al. v. Gilmore, No. 97-1390 (A-738); In re Breard, No. 97-8660 (A-767); Republic of Paraguay et al. v. Gilmore, No. 125 Original (A-771). Applications decided April 14, 1998, before the execution scheduled for 9 p.m.; October Term 1997, chunk 6. No oral argument is recorded for these applications.

A-738 seeks a stay or affirmative injunction pending review of the Fourth Circuit's January 22, 1998 civil judgment, 134 F.3d 622. Paraguay, its Ambassador and Consul General assert their own Vienna Convention and 1859 Friendship Treaty rights; the Consul General also pleaded §1983. The lower court affirmed on immunity grounds, treating the notice violation as completed and the requested relief as retrospective. It did not decide the alternative Rooker-Feldman or political-question defenses. The Fourth Circuit application is presented to Chief Justice Stone-Zsela and by him referred to the Court under its standing practice.

A-767 accompanies an original habeas petition under §§2241 and 2254. It asks for a stay pending disposition of that petition. Time for ICJ consideration and this Court's consideration of the United States' response are the stated purposes, not an automatic extension through the international merits proceeding. The applicant offers certiorari-stay and preliminary-injunction tests expressly as analogies. A-771 accompanies the April 13 motion for leave to file an original complaint invoking Article III and §1251(b)(1); it seeks a temporary restraining order or preliminary injunction on the asserted newly threatened breach of the April 9 ICJ measure, Charter obligations, comity and the Consul General's official-capacity §1983 claim. Both original requests are before the Court as original filings; neither is recited as a circuit referral.

The ICJ proceeding began April 3. Its April 9 provisional measure asks the United States to take all measures at its disposal to prevent execution pending its final decision and to inform the ICJ of measures taken. Its preliminary jurisdiction and urgency determinations reserve the treaty remedy and the relevance of prejudice. The present questions concern immediate domestic protection through three distinct channels. A-732 is not decided in this order; neither certiorari petition, the original habeas petition nor the original-action leave motion receives a final disposition.

Date provenance is the validated April 14 application setting, before the scheduled execution. The proposed April 16 protection endpoints in the frozen dissenting commitments are new proposed judicial choices, not recovered events or entered orders. They become no continuation clock because no such protection receives five votes. No execution, clemency act, executive refusal, return, service default, expired stay or subsequent ICJ development is presumed. The lower Breard habeas decision is dated January 20; the Paraguay civil decision January 22. Collateral discrepant recitals in the stay application do not change those supported dates.

## Participation, channels and entering law

Chief Justice Stone-Zsela and Justices Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer participate at submission and decision. No recusal, absence or substitution is established.

All nine participate, satisfying the six-Justice quorum. The application threshold is five of nine, not certiorari's Rule of Four. A-738 follows the actual Fourth Circuit allotment to Stone-Zsela and the standing referral practice. A-767 is original habeas under Rule 20.4 and §§2241/2254/2251; A-771 is an originally filed civil request under Rules 17 and 21 with the Article III/§1251(b)(1) assertion. Original filing is not converted into circuit business from Virginia's location. No separate individual recipient, substitution or individual temporary action is invented for those filings. Every participating Justice supplies signed reasons for all three components, and the Chief certifies the compound order; certification supplies no additional vote or ground.

Rule 23 preserves its ordinary prior-resort requirement and extraordinary-circumstances exception; no source gap establishes failure. Rule 20.4 preserves exceptional circumstances, absence of adequate alternative relief, reasons for bypassing district court and exhaustion or the applicable §2254(b) alternative. Section 2254(b)(1)'s absent/ineffective-state-process alternatives remain; (b)(2) permits, rather than requires, merits denial despite nonexhaustion; (b)(3) requires counsel's express waiver. None is factually resolved here. Original habeas is ex parte unless a show-cause response is ordered. Filing or docketing creates neither automatic relief nor a merits determination.

Entering-law authorities are the exact relevant reading selections in [chunk 6 B](../entering-law/OT_1997CHUNK6_B.md), [Blessing](../entering-law/chunk6_b_blessing.md), [Steel Co.](../entering-law/chunk6_b_steel_co.md) and [Baker](../entering-law/chunk6_b_baker_public.md), supplemented by the seven earlier-effective public copies in `../entering-law/chunk6_intervening_public/`. Coleman, Felker, Lonchar, the Seminole and Coeur d'Alene rules, Trest, Triestman and Aktepe retain their precise authority and reservations. Woodard's clemency minimum neither supplies a treaty cause nor makes mercy exclusive. The other intervening decisions, including Hinds, change no treaty, interim-relief or original-jurisdiction rule. No later precedent or later event enters the decision.

## Stone: approved core and final compatibility

The scoped [Stone supplement](../runtime/CHUNK6_SCOPED/breard_v_greene_STONE.md), approved October 21, 2026, controls his personal disposition. This assembly received it only after the completed reconciled freeze. The approved core denies each requested emergency protection after separate vehicle-specific inquiry; it reserves categorical treaty enforceability, ultimate prejudice and the final accompanying proceedings. It requires independent original consideration under Felker, prohibits the automatic successive-authorization bar, finds no sufficient exceptional-original-relief showing or identified unfinished legally required process, and requires Paraguay's actual domestic duty, right, channel and remedy without importing historical categorical immunity. The core supplies his complete signed explanation for the three completed applications. No standing fallback is used.

The supplemental source law does not alter an established factual premise or require Stone to make the denied relief available: it identifies lawful preservation authority and a disputed necessity application. His fixed denial of emergency protection remains intact on his approved independent showing ground. He is not attributed a decision about §2283 party/privity, personal §1983 entitlement, necessary aid, a new anti-injunction exception or colleagues' specific preservation analysis. No new burden or reason is needed, and no material narrowing or broader full-opinion join is authorized or made. His public statement preserves all three distinct channels and all reservations. The opinion's A-771 new-duty assessment is not a disguised decision on the past notice claim.

A-732 is not assembled. Its separate proportionality-process ground lacks an approved Stone reason and sufficiently verified lower treatment. The treaty-ground denial cannot silently resolve that different ground. This is a blocker for A-732 only, not for these three distinct applications; no A-732 vote or disposition is published by this Record.

## Form, final compatibility and assignment

The [form-first receipt](../runtime/OT_1997CHUNK6_BREARD_ASSEMBLY_VALIDATION.md) fixes one compound procedural order with distinct application components, a common signed Associate explanation, Stone's signed explanation, Scalia's additional ground and the two component-specific short-protection dissents before counts or authors were considered. One instrument fits the common execution emergency while retaining separate vehicles, votes, grounds and relief; it does not consolidate the underlying proceedings. One eligible author can carry the complete common Associate explanation, so no division among authors is needed. These application writings do not count as plenary merits leads.

Stone assigns the common Associate explanation because he supports the denial of each application. His separate Circuit-Justice duty for A-738 arises from the allotment, not this assignment. The scratch recount from actual baseline opinion topologies and the seven intervening Records' opinion tables gives **Stone-Zsela 5; Stevens 6; O'Connor 7; Scalia 6; Kennedy 6; Souter 6; Thomas 6; Ginsburg 7; Breyer 6**. Total: 55. Last counted event: United States v. Hinds, April 6, 1998, Stevens. Texas remains an uncounted threshold disposition; excluded procedural, per curiam, summary and separate writings supply no increment. The [recount receipt](../runtime/OT_1997CHUNK6_BREARD_ASSIGNMENT_RECOUNT.json) retains all actual source topologies and individual author increments; no earlier tally supplies a count.

Eligible authors for the entire common explanation are O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas, whose reconciled commitments join every proposition in all three parts. The eligible minimum is six and the ceiling seven; all four are in the pool: O'Connor (7), Scalia (6), Kennedy (6), Thomas (6). Stone's independent core does not adopt the complete additional analysis, Souter opposes the A-771 denial, and Stevens, Ginsburg and Breyer oppose A-767 and A-771 denials. These are actual scope limits, not capability exclusions.

Kennedy writes. His Lucas opinion distinguishes protection of an identified enforceable duty from irreparability alone, and his Aktepe opinion separates a manageable legal command from a foreign-relations label. Those date-eligible grounds fit the common opinion's principal work: retain lawful avenues while explaining why the particular domestic duty/remedy showing and administrative necessity are insufficient. O'Connor is the strongest alternative through her Felker extraordinary-channel analysis, but that habeas ground is already shared; Kennedy's own affirmative-injunction and specific-duty reasoning more directly coordinates the two distinct civil requests and their limits, with the lower count. No expansion accommodation or changed commitment is invented. Scalia's additional injunction formulation remains separate. Stevens writes the two short-protection dissents on the exact common grounds adopted by their stated joiners; their form preserves his Lonchar meaningful-consideration distinction without creating mandatory process. No writing adds a count; the total remains 55.

No Associate changes a reconciled disposition, ground or duration at assembly. The A-738 changes of Stevens, Ginsburg and Breyer occurred in the separate clean supplemental-model freeze before reconciliation and before Stone exposure. No reply to Stone, imagined draft exchange or new personal reservation supplies a join. The complete A-738 opinion has eight direct joins, A-767 five, and A-771 four. Stone's independently expressed A-771 common interim proposition provides a fifth direct supporter only for Holding IV; this is not a whole-opinion join or a Marks logical-subset inference. The administrative proponents oppose immediate denial but do not support the full longer relief. All 27 application positions reconcile to the three announced votes.

## Public action, judgments and opinion table

The Court denies A-738, A-767 and A-771. No stay or injunction issues through these applications. The votes and the participating Justices' signed positions and adopted reasons appear below. The accompanying proceedings remain pending.

The foregoing order records the action of the Court. The participating Justices' positions and the reasons they adopt are set out below. Certified for issuance: Chief Justice Alex-Lamar Stone-Zsela, April 14, 1998.

| Application | Action and vote | Supporting denial | Opposing denial | Immediate effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-738, No. 97-1390 | Stay or injunction denied, 9–0 | Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer | — | No execution restraint; the civil judgment is undisturbed at this stage; certiorari remains pending |
| A-767, No. 97-8660 | Execution stay denied, 6–3 | Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas | Stevens, Ginsburg, Breyer | No stay; original habeas remains pending |
| A-771, No. 125 Original | Temporary restraining order or preliminary injunction denied, 5–4 | Stone-Zsela, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Thomas | Stevens, Souter, Ginsburg, Breyer | No injunction; leave to file remains pending |

Opposition to denial is confined to short administrative protection. Stevens, Ginsburg and Breyer would grant only a §2251 administrative stay in A-767 until 5 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time on April 16, 1998, or an earlier further Court order, reserving the remainder. Stevens, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer would grant only an administrative injunction in A-771 with that endpoint, subject also to earlier vacation if the relevant want of jurisdiction or injunctive power is determined. They would reserve the longer request and leave motion. Those proposals do not grant the full requested relief and are not orders of the Court. These denials neither command execution nor find that execution occurred; they grant no writ, review, vacatur, release, remand, response deadline or hearing.

| Writing | Author | Joined by | Relationship and scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opinion of the Court, Part I | Kennedy | Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer | Complete A-738 interim duty/remedy ground and separate rejection of a further administrative interval; eight direct joins |
| Opinion of the Court, Part II | Kennedy | O'Connor, Scalia, Souter, Thomas | Complete A-767 extraordinary-habeas and unfinished-process grounds; five direct joins |
| Opinion announcing the A-771 denial, Part III | Kennedy | O'Connor, Scalia, Thomas | Domestic-enforcement showing and additional rejection of the proposed necessary-aid interval; four joins to the complete explanation |
| Signed explanation concurring in the three denials | Stone-Zsela | No other Justice | Own interim grounds; Circuit Justice's explanation for A-738, and individual statements for A-767 and A-771; no join in Kennedy's complete opinion or additional §2283 analysis |
| Concurrence | Scalia | No other Justice | Joins Kennedy's three parts and adds his affirmative-injunction ground for A-738 and A-771 only |
| Dissent from denial of A-767 | Stevens | Ginsburg, Breyer | Only the defined §2251 administrative stay; no longer-stay or original-writ disposition |
| Dissent from denial of A-771 | Stevens | Souter, Ginsburg, Breyer | Only the defined original-jurisdiction preservation injunction under §1651 and §2283's necessary-aid exception |

No complete A-771 opinion commands a majority. The limited interim proposition identified in Holding IV is independently supported by Kennedy, O'Connor, Scalia and Thomas and by Stone-Zsela's separate explanation. That express agreement supplies five votes for that proposition, without treating Stone-Zsela as joining Part III's additional analysis or combining incompatible rationales under Marks.

## Controlling holdings

### I. A-738 does not establish the necessary prospect of prospective relief for a current consular violation

**Holding and operative rule:** Even assuming the invoked notice duties were binding and violated, and applying the applicants' favorable formulation requiring a reasonable probability that four Justices would grant review, a significant possibility of reversal, likely irreparable harm and appropriate consideration of competing equities, A-738 does not establish the necessary prospect that the older consular duties require the requested execution restraint as relief for a current violation. A continuing consequence of past nonnotification is not by itself a continuing denial of these applicants' presently available consular rights; the distinct most-favored-consul notification theory does not itself establish the requested remedy.

**Authority:** Kennedy's Part I, joined by all seven other Associate Justices, supplies eight direct joins to this complete rule and application. Stone-Zsela independently agrees that the current domestic duty and remedial showing is insufficient, without adopting the complete explanation.

**Controlling explanation:** The Court considers Paraguay's own rights, not a supposed default of Breard's personal claim. Article 36 protects communication and access; consular notification must occur without delay if the national requests it, while advice to the national and forwarding covered communications must also occur without delay. It protects visits, correspondence and arranging representation, including after judgment, but requires consular officers to abstain from action on the national's behalf if the national expressly opposes that action. Its receiving-State-law clause is qualified by the requirement that those laws give full effect to the rights' purposes. Neither half may be omitted.

The most-favored-consul provision of the 1859 Treaty supports a distinct notification theory without the same request condition. Even accepting that theory for this inquiry, consular access has been available since 1996. The current presentation does not sufficiently connect the old omission to a present duty requiring this execution restraint.

Young supplies prospective officer relief for an ongoing federal violation. Seminole and Coeur d'Alene preserve that route within actual duties and remedies; they remove categorical immunity shortcuts without supplying this treaty remedy. Papasan and Milliken permit relief for a legally continuing violation produced by past events, but not every continuing harm establishes a current violation of each claimant's right. The full-effect argument therefore deserves consideration but does not establish the required interim prospect. Irreversibility and the international interests are material, not substitutes for that showing. The Court decides neither the ultimate treaty remedy nor a categorical immunity rule, and does not import A-771's newly pleaded ICJ duty into this older claim.

**Precedent treatment:** Young, Seminole and Coeur d'Alene retain the connected-officer, ongoing-duty and prospective-remedy boundaries; Papasan and Milliken retain the distinction between a continuing violation and continuing effects. Coleman supplies the separate review/reversal/irreparability framework used on the applicants' favorable assumption; no universal full-Court affirmative-injunction standard is selected.

### II. A-738's older civil claim requires no further protected jurisdictional interval

**Holding and operative rule:** A-738 also supplies no basis for an administrative execution injunction merely to obtain additional coordinated consideration of the older treaty claim. Even assuming an otherwise lawful §2283 route in the applicants' favor, that claim's interim duty-and-remedy question can be assessed now; no necessary additional jurisdictional or injunctive-power inquiry is established by the prospect that execution-specific relief will become unavailable.

**Authority:** Kennedy's Part I has all eight Associate Justices. Stone-Zsela denies interim relief on his own stated ground and does not adopt this additional analysis.

**Controlling explanation:** Shipp and United Mine Workers permit necessary preservation while a court determines a substantial question about its authority. They do not require delay whenever further consideration is desired, and restraint must cease if the relevant want of power is determined. Pennsylvania Bureau of Correction keeps §1651 auxiliary and subordinate to specifically governing statutes.

Hill and Atlantic Coast Line treat enforcement of a state judgment, including ministerial execution, as a state proceeding for §2283. Directing an order to officers, giving it a short duration or calling it administrative supplies no exception. The exceptions are express congressional authorization, necessity in aid of the issuing court's jurisdiction, and protection or effectuation of its judgments. The ICJ measure is not this Court's judgment, and foreign sovereignty does not confer the United States-plaintiff exception.

Hale and County of Imperial preserve a genuinely independent nonparty route, but absence from a caption does not decide party or privity status. Mitchum classifies §1983 as expressly authorized; a pleaded theory still requires the particular right, defendant and interim showing. It does not attach the Consul General's exception automatically to Paraguay's separate claims. Those predicates remain unresolved, not decided against applicants.

Even favorable answers would not supply the missing interim showing or need for another interval here. The jurisdiction at issue is review of a federal civil judgment. Atlantic Coast Line's distinct discussion of potential Supreme Court review of state decisions does not turn this civil petition into review of Virginia's criminal judgment. The older claim is presently assessable; the new original claim has its own channel. No general exception from §2283, factual default, political-question bar or final merits adjudication on assumed Article III jurisdiction follows.

**Precedent treatment:** Shipp and United Mine Workers retain necessary, substantial-question preservation; Pennsylvania Bureau preserves statutory limits; Hill and Atlantic Coast Line govern the restraint's character and exceptions; Hale, County of Imperial and Mitchum retain their distinct coverage and authorization routes without a present finding satisfying or defeating them.

### III. A-767 does not warrant a stay through the original-habeas channel

**Holding and operative rule:** After independent consideration of the retained original-habeas route, A-767 presents no sufficiently substantial prospect of extraordinary domestic habeas relief and identifies no unfinished process actually required by governing law that demands interim protection. The stay is denied without denying the original petition, treating the new ICJ order as a defaulted or previously adjudicated claim, or finding an unverified Rule 20 condition unsatisfied.

**Authority:** Kennedy's Part II is joined by O'Connor, Scalia, Souter and Thomas: five direct joins to the complete explanation. Stone-Zsela separately adopts the insufficient-exceptional-relief and no-identified-required-process grounds, supplying a sixth denial vote without joining every additional proposition.

**Controlling explanation:** Felker preserves original habeas under §2241 independently of review of successive-application authorization. Circuit permission is not a prerequisite here. Rule 20 nevertheless requires exceptional circumstances, no adequate relief elsewhere, reasons for not applying to the district court, and exhaustion or the §2254(b) alternatives of unavailable state corrective process or circumstances rendering that process ineffective. Sections 2244(b)(1)–(2) inform discretion; their direct mandatory force in this channel remains reserved. The Court assumes unresolved procedural matters favorably for this interim inquiry rather than inventing nonexhaustion or waiver.

The April 9 measure receives separate consideration. Even assuming international bindingness, its preservation of an interstate dispute does not on this showing establish a sufficiently substantial personal domestic custody claim. Compulsory international jurisdiction, Charter Article 94's compliance undertaking, Statute Article 41's provisional authority and a domestic habeas remedy are distinct questions. Comity does not itself create that custody right or enlarge §2251. The ICJ reserved the treaty remedy and prejudice; notice failure and the disputed plea counterfactual establish neither causal prejudice nor an innocence gateway or hearing entitlement. The earlier treaty claim retains its own defenses, which are not mechanically attached to the new order.

Section 2251 permits a stay of state proceedings involving the detained person and a matter in pending habeas before final judgment, after a judgment of discharge, or pending appeal; filing alone suspends nothing. Lonchar protects an identified legally required opportunity when lawful expedition cannot finish before execution. No such unfinished obligation is identified here, and Rule 20 makes an original petition ex parte unless a response is required. The serious new-duty argument does not require another compulsory step before this interim decision. The Court neither settles every domestic enforcement question nor converts the application's stated ICJ purposes into an automatic stay through international merits.

**Precedent treatment:** Felker's retained channel, extraordinary showing and original-§2244 reservation remain intact; Lonchar's necessary-process trigger is applied without an automatic hearing or stay; Schlup's new-evidence gateway remains distinct from notice failure and ordinary prejudice. The certiorari and civil-injunction analogies offered in the application do not replace the original-habeas inquiry.

### IV. A-771 lacks the present domestic showing for its requested interim injunction

**Holding and operative rule:** A-771's emergency submission does not sufficiently establish the domestic right, ongoing duty, jurisdictional route and remedy needed for the requested injunction through the proposed original action. Denial resolves immediate protection only: the Court reserves categorical treaty enforceability, ultimate prejudice, final original jurisdiction, the separate cause-of-action questions and the leave motion.

**Authority:** Kennedy, O'Connor, Scalia and Thomas expressly adopt this interim insufficiency proposition in Part III; Stone-Zsela independently adopts the same proposition in his signed explanation. These five directly support it at this limited level. No whole opinion or additional §2283 necessity application has five denial-coalition joins, and no Marks synthesis supplies one.

**Controlling explanation:** The Court must examine the domestic channel and showing for Paraguay's own request. The new asserted preservation obligation receives its own interim assessment; denial is not a declaration that the earlier notification omission exhausts every later claim. A serious international obligation and the gravity of execution are material, but neither by itself supplies an enforceable domestic right, an ongoing duty against the named officers or authority for the particular remedy.

Seminole preserves a prospective officer route in its statutory setting and leaves direct-State amenability without a controlling rationale. It therefore supplies neither the categorical immunity ground urged from a broader account of that decision nor a treaty cause of action for these applicants. The present submission does not sufficiently establish the needed domestic injunction through the original proceeding. The Court denies the immediate request while leaving final cause-of-action and original-jurisdiction questions for their own determination. The four-Justice statutory-preservation objection and the four-Justice contrary preservation analysis remain separate positions; neither becomes the Court's additional rationale merely because five Justices agree on denial.

**Precedent treatment:** Seminole's officer holding and unresolved direct-State question are preserved, without categorical immunity or an automatic treaty cause. No new controlling construction of §2283, Article 94, Article 41, §1983 personhood or international provisional-measure enforceability results from this limited shared ground.

## Precedent and current force
